items.title: PIDSMaker
items.text:
Build, benchmark and extend graph-based intrusion detection systems.

State-of-the-art provenance and network IDSs, their datasets and one modular pipeline, all open source.

Get started Quickstart GitHub Discord

Runs on Linux (GPU or CPU) macOS (Apple Silicon)

items.title: Up and running in two commands
items.text: From v5.0.0, PIDSMaker needs no database server or Docker: datasets are downloaded from Hugging Face on first use.

items.title: One framework, two views
items.text:
• Provenance

    System events inside each host: processes, files and netflows. Provenance-based IDSs (Velox, Orthrus, Kairos, MAGIC...) on DARPA TC, OpTC, ATLASv2 and CARBANAKv2, detecting the entities of an attack.

    Provenance graphs

  • Network

    Authentications and flows between hosts. Network IDSs (Euler, Argus, Jbeil, LARES...) on LANL and the network flows of OpTC, detecting the malicious events of lateral movement.

    Network graphs

Both go through the same seven stages and share the same components, so most systems run on either kind of data, and a new idea can be tested on both.

items.title: Why PIDSMaker?
items.text:
Papers at top security venues often evaluate on the same datasets, but each uses its own labels and its own implementation of the baselines, so their results can't be compared fairly. PIDSMaker gives the community one framework, maintained in the open, that fixes this.

  • Fair benchmarking: state-of-the-art baselines evaluated with the same datasets, labels and reference implementations.
  • Modular components: the components of published systems, extracted into a testbed where you mix and match them to discover better variants.
  • Shared code: a central place where authors contribute their systems, so new work can be benchmarked reproducibly.

items.title: Next steps
items.text:
Run other systems Download datasets Make it yours

Run any system on a provenance or a network dataset, by name:

pidsmaker velox CADETS_E3          # a provenance IDS
pidsmaker euler LANL               # a network IDS
pidsmaker kairos THEIA_E3 --wandb  # logged to Weights & Biases

All the datasets are Parquet files in the Hugging Face repository pidsmaker/datasets, from 0.16 GB (ATLASV2_EDR) to 74 GB (TRACE_E5), 178 GB in total. A run downloads its dataset when it is missing, or you can download datasets ahead of time:

pidsmaker download CADETS_E3 LANL  # some datasets
pidsmaker download --list          # all the datasets and their sizes

Runs on Linux, ideally with an NVIDIA NVIDIA GPU, for all datasets, and on macOS (Apple Silicon), on CPU, for most datasets: 32 GB of RAM is ideal (details).

Override any argument from the CLI, or write a new YAML config that inherits from an existing system.

pidsmaker orthrus CADETS_E3 \
  --featurization.used_method=doc2vec \
  --training.encoder.used_methods=tgn,sage \
  --training.encoder.sage.num_layers=3

items.title: Contributing
items.text:
PIDSMaker aims to keep up with the latest research on provenance-based and network intrusion detection, and it can only do so with the help of the community. Every contribution is welcome!

  • Talk to us first

    Questions, ideas, or a contribution to discuss before starting? Join the Discord.

  • Report a bug

    Open an issue on GitHub with the command you ran and the error.

items.title: What to contribute
items.text:
• A new system: your published PIDS or NIDS, so that others can benchmark against it. Start with the tutorial.
  • New components: encoders, decoders, objectives, featurization methods, provenance or network datasets...
  • Fixes to existing systems: some systems may not perfectly reflect their original implementation.
  • Bug fixes and optimizations: spotted a slow operation and found a better alternative? Send it!
  • Documentation: typos, unclear explanations, missing examples. Every page has an edit button.

items.title: Development tips
items.text: Install from source Clone the repository and install it in editable mode, with the test dependencies: pip install -e ".[test]" (see Installation). Your changes are used without reinstalling. Avoid concurrent runs from scratch Two runs started at the same time with the same construction arguments on the same dataset write to the same folder, which can silently corrupt their outputs. Start the first run, wait until the shared tasks are done, then launch the others. Alternatively, use --restart_from_scratch. See Caching of tasks. Iterate quickly Use a small dataset such as CLEARSCOPE_E3 or CADETS_E3, and --force_restart=TASK to re-run only the task you are changing.

items.title: Before opening a pull request
items.text:
1. Format the code. The repository uses ruff through pre-commit: 
    pre-commit run --all-files
  2. Run the tests. Functional tests check that changes to one component don't break the others. Update them when you add a component. They run the pipeline in test mode on a small sample of CLEARSCOPE_E3 (tests/fixtures/), written as a temporary Parquet dataset: they need neither the full datasets nor a database server. === "GPU" 
    pytest tests -n 4                       # in parallel with pytest-xdist
    === "CPU" 
    pytest tests -n 4 --device cpu          # as in the CI
    === "Full dataset" 
    pytest tests -n 4 --db full             # CLEARSCOPE_E3 tests on the full dataset
    === "Coverage" 
    pytest --cov=pidsmaker tests/
    The tests also run on CPU with GitHub Actions on every pull request (.github/workflows/tests.yml), on Python 3.9 and 3.11. See tests/README.md for all options.
  3. Update the documentation. If you added or changed arguments in pidsmaker/config/config.py, regenerate the reference and check the docs locally (see below).

items.title: Building the documentation
items.text:
The documentation is built with Zensical from the docs/ folder. Zensical needs Python ≥ 3.10 (≥ 3.11 for the version used by the CI, 0.1.3). With a PIDSMaker environment in Python 3.11, install it there:

pip install zensical

With a PIDSMaker environment in Python 3.9 or 3.10, install Zensical in a separate environment with Python ≥ 3.11.

Then, with PIDSMaker installed from source (the argument reference is generated by importing pidsmaker):

cd docs
./build.sh                          # regenerate the argument reference, then build
zensical serve -a 0.0.0.0:8000      # live preview on http://localhost:8000/PIDSMaker/

Zensical reports broken links and anchors at every build: please fix them before opening your pull request.

What Where Pages docs/docs/**/*.md Navigation, theme, redirects docs/zensical.toml Styles docs/docs/stylesheets/extra.css Generated argument lists docs/scripts/args/, produced by docs/scripts/get_arguments.py

The site is deployed to GitHub Pages automatically when changes are merged into main.

items.title: Releasing a new version
items.text:
Maintainers release a version in two steps:

  1. In a pull request, set version in pyproject.toml (e.g. 5.1.0), update the release notes table of the README, and write the notes of the GitHub release in .github/releases/5.1.0.md.
  2. Once it is merged, run the workflow from Actions > publish > Run workflow, on main, with the version 5.1.0.

The workflow (.github/workflows/publish.yml) checks that the version is the one of pyproject.toml and that it is not released yet. Then it builds the package and publishes it to PyPI, creates the tag and the GitHub release (with the notes of .github/releases/<version>.md, or the list of the merged pull requests if there is no such file), and announces it on Discord. PyPI trusts this workflow as a trusted publisher, so no token is stored in the repository.

A release published from the GitHub page, with a tag equal to the version of pyproject.toml, is also published to PyPI.

items.title: FAQ & troubleshooting
items.text: Answers to the questions that come up most often. Can't find yours? Ask on Discord or open an issue.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
Do I need a database server?

No. PIDSMaker installs with pip, and reads its datasets from Parquet files with DuckDB, in the Python process.

pip refuses to install PIDSMaker, or can't find torch==2.1.2.

Check the version of Python: PIDSMaker needs Python 3.9 to 3.11, as PyTorch 2.1.2 has no wheels for Python 3.12 and later. Create the environment with conda create -n pids python=3.11.

Which datasets should I start with?

For provenance-based detection, CADETS_E3, THEIA_E3 and CLEARSCOPE_E3. They are small (0.5 to 1.3 GB), quick to process, and the most used in papers. For network detection, LANL. E5 datasets and TRACE_E3 are much larger: see the sizes in the installation guide.

A dataset download stopped halfway.

Run the same pidsmaker download command again: downloads resume where they stopped. A run whose dataset is incomplete also downloads the missing files.

A run doesn't find a dataset I downloaded, or downloads it again.

The run looks for datasets in another folder than the one you downloaded them to. Both use --datasets_dir, else $PIDSMAKER_DATASETS_DIR, else ~/.cache/pidsmaker/datasets: set PIDSMAKER_DATASETS_DIR once, e.g. in your ~/.bashrc, rather than passing --datasets_dir to some commands only. See Where files are stored.

The embedding visualizer fails with address already in use on port 5000.

Another program uses this port, e.g. AirPlay Receiver on macOS. Start the embedding visualizer on another port with --port.

A run is killed (Killed, exit code 137) on a laptop.

The run ran out of memory: runs on provenance datasets can take more than 15 GB of RAM (see macOS). Graph construction uses less memory with fewer processes, e.g. --num_workers=2.

items.title: Running experiments
items.text:
I don't have a GPU.

PIDSMaker falls back to the CPU automatically, with a warning. You can also force it with --cpu. Expect much longer training times on large datasets.

A system fails on a dataset of the other family.
  • Flash and ThreaTrace predict node types (predict_node_type), which needs at least two node types, and R-Caid predicts the executables of processes (predict_process_tag): they can't run on network datasets, which only have hosts.
  • Argus, LARES, E-GraphSAGE and Anomal-E use the attributes of events, which provenance datasets don't have: add --batching.edge_features=edge_type.

See Running across families.

I changed the code, but the task is skipped.

Tasks are cached under a hash of their arguments, not of the code. After changing the code of a task, re-run it with --force_restart=TASK (e.g. --force_restart=training). See Forcing a restart.

Where are the outputs of my runs?

In the artifact folder: $PIDSMAKER_ARTIFACT_DIR if it is set, else /home/artifacts/ if this folder exists, else artifacts/ in the folder where you started the run. Use --artifact_dir to change it for a run. See Where files are stored.

My disk is full.

Each run caches the outputs of every task, which can exceed 15 GB per run on E3 datasets. Point PIDSMAKER_ARTIFACT_DIR to a large disk, and delete the folders of old experiments. Runs started with --restart_from_scratch delete their outputs automatically at the end.

Can I run several experiments in parallel?

Yes. With simple architectures, 3 to 4 runs fit on a single A100 GPU without major overhead. Start each of them with --background, which runs it detached from the terminal, with its own log file. Avoid starting several runs with the same early tasks at the same time: they would write to the same folder. See Caching of tasks.

The GPU runs out of memory.

Reduce the size of the graphs or batches (e.g. construction.time_window_size, or the batching arguments in Batching & sampling), or the embedding sizes (training.node_hid_dim, training.node_out_dim).

I don't want to use Weights & Biases.

Run pidsmaker SYSTEM DATASET without --wandb: metrics are printed in the logs.

items.title: Results
items.text:
I get very different results from one run to the next, or from the papers.

This is expected: self-supervised detectors, PIDSs and NIDSs alike, are unstable, and small changes of seed or hyperparameters change their results a lot. Run each configuration several times with --experiment=run_n_times and report the mean and standard deviation; see Instability. Also check that you use the same ground truth as the paper you compare with.

Which configuration should I use to compare with an existing system?

Mind data snooping: orthrus and velox don't use test data during training, but some other configs keep the original settings of their system, which do. See Systems. For network systems, also read Comparing NIDSs with published results.

items.title: Features
items.text:
predict_edge_supervised complains that attack embeddings are missing.

The attack labels are embedded by the feat_inference task. If it was already run with the same settings (e.g. by pretrained_velox), it is skipped: add --force_restart=feat_inference. See Supervised fine-tuning.

Llama pretrained encoders fail to download.

Llama models are gated on Hugging Face: accept the license on the model page, then run huggingface-cli login where PIDSMaker runs.

The embedding visualizer page doesn't load on localhost.

If 127.0.0.1 works but localhost doesn't, the server listens on IPv4 only while localhost resolves to IPv6. Start it with --host ::. See Embedding visualizer.

items.title: Adversarial attacks
items.text:
How robust is a detector to an attacker who tries to blend in? PIDSMaker can modify the data to simulate attacks, at three different stages of the pipeline.

Attack What changes Stage Argument Mimicry attack Benign-looking file activity is added to the attack processes, in the test graphs Construction construction.mimicry_edge_num Synthetic attacks Fake attacks are injected in the training and validation graphs, labeled for few-shot detection Transformation transformation.used_methods: synthetic_attack_naive Renaming attack Attack processes get the embedding of a benign name Feature inference feat_inference.rename_attack

Provenance datasets only

The three simulations act on provenance activity: they add file accesses and connections of processes with the event types of DARPA TC, or rename processes. They don't apply to network datasets.

items.title: Mimicry attack
items.text:
A mimicry attack hides malicious processes by making them behave like benign ones: on top of the attack, they perform ordinary file accesses, which dilutes the anomaly that the detector learned to spot.

With construction.mimicry_edge_num set to N > 0, PIDSMaker adds N such events to the attacks of the dataset, split evenly between them. For each attack:

  1. Attack processes. The attack's nodes are taken from the ground truth. Its entry points (the attack nodes without incoming events) and the processes reachable from them during the attack's time range are used as attack processes.
  2. Benign-looking events. Until the quota is reached, a random attack process opens a random file of the dataset and performs one of 14 typical sequences of reads and writes, at a time when the process was active, a few seconds apart.
  3. Injection. The events are added to the graph of the day of the attack. They are not written to the database.
  4. Ground truth. The processes and files used are saved in the mimicry/ folder of the construction task, and added to the ground truth as attack nodes, so evaluation checks whether the detector still finds them.
pidsmaker orthrus CADETS_E3 --construction.mimicry_edge_num=1000

Compare the metrics with those of the same run without mimicry (mimicry_edge_num: 0, the default in every system). Since it is a construction argument, the whole pipeline runs again.

Limitations

  • The generated events use the event types of DARPA TC: use mimicry on the E3 and E5 datasets only.
  • It is not supported with the threatrace ground truth, nor with construction.used_method: magic.
  • The injected events are added after the real events of the day, so they end up in the last time-window graph of the day rather than in the windows of their timestamps.

items.title: Synthetic attacks
items.text:
synthetic_attack_naive injects simple, labeled attacks in the training and validation graphs, so that a detector can learn from attack examples (few-shot detection). Test graphs are left unchanged.

  1. It selects num_malicious_process processes that receive network data (EVENT_RECVFROM) in both the training and validation graphs. The only selection method is random.
  2. In up to num_attacks graphs where each process appears, it adds unauthorized accesses (EVENT_OPEN, EVENT_READ, EVENT_WRITE) to num_unauthorized_file_access files that the process never accessed, then a connection (EVENT_CONNECT) to a network node, as an exfiltration.
  3. Injected edges are labeled as attacks (y = 1). They are removed from self-supervised training, and used by the few-shot objective (training.decoder.use_few_shot).
pidsmaker orthrus CADETS_E3 \
  --transformation.used_methods=synthetic_attack_naive \
  --transformation.synthetic_attack_naive.num_malicious_process=10

Note

synthetic_attack_naive must be the only transformation, and its labels are only used by few-shot training, a legacy feature. Evaluation always uses the real ground truth. To train a detector with attack examples, prefer the supervised fine-tuning objective.

items.title: Renaming attack
items.text: Attackers often rename their malware after a benign program. With pretrained encoders, which embed entities from their names, feat_inference.rename_attack simulates this at inference time: the embedding of each attack process is replaced by the embedding of a frequent benign name. See Renaming attack.

items.title: Batching & sampling
items.text:
Batching refers to grouping edges, nodes, or graphs into a temporal graph provided as input to the model.

We provide three batching strategies that can be configured via dedicated batching arguments.

Global Batching: takes as input a large flattened graph comprising all events in the dataset and partitions it into equal-size graphs based on number of edges, minutes, or similar.

Intra-graph Batching: applies similar batching as global batching but within each built graph.

Inter-graph Batching: groups multiple graphs into a single batch. This batch is a large graph where all graphs are stacked together without any overlap, following the mini-batching strategy from PyG.

Note

All three batching strategies apply sequentially and can be used together.

items.title: Choosing the Right Batch Size
items.text:
The batch size plays a key role in determining the trade-off between memory usage, speed, and learning effectiveness. Selecting an appropriate batch size requires careful consideration of the graph’s scale, the temporal dynamics, and the available hardware resources.

Large Batches

  • ✅ Enhance training speed through better GPU parallelization
  • ✅ Capture events over longer time periods
  • ❌ Increase GPU memory usage
  • ❌ May cause high node in-degree, leading to over-squashing (loss of neighbor information)

Small Batches

  • ✅ Reduce GPU memory consumption
  • ✅ Enable fine-grained neighborhood aggregation
  • ❌ Extend training time
  • ❌ Risk missing graph patterns spanning longer time ranges if temporal features are not captured

items.title: TGN Last Neighbor Sampling
items.text:
In the Temporal Graph Network (TGN) architecture, the objective is to predict edges within a graph batch at time t based on the last neighbors of each node seen in batches happening prior to t. Setting tgn_last_neighbor to the argument batching.intra_graph_batching.used_methods enables to pre-compute the TGN graph for each preprocessed graph in the dataset. Specifically, it does not replace the graph directly but adds tgn_* attributes to it, which can be used by the downstream encoder.

To use the TGN architecture, you should also add tgn to training.encoder.used_methods as it enables to properly handle TGN attributes. The TGNEncoder accepts as argument an encoder, defined in the config, which will be applied to the pre-computed TGN graph.

Examples of TGN config can be found in kairos.yml and orthrus.yml (provenance), and jbeil.yml (network).

With tgn_last_neighbor.negative_destinations, a negative destination is drawn for each edge, uniformly among the destinations of the training graphs (or of all graphs, for validation and test), and embedded by the TGN with the nodes of the batch, as in TGN and Jbeil. It is used by the tgn negative sampling of predict_edge_contrastive (see jbeil.yml).

items.title: Instability
items.text: Systems trained with self-supervised learning, provenance-based (PIDSs) and network (NIDSs) alike, exhibit significant instability—that is, high sensitivity to training perturbations. Running the same configuration with different random seeds or minor hyperparameter changes often yields substantially different detection performance.

items.title: Why are these systems unstable?
items.text:
Several factors contribute to this instability:

  1. Self-supervised learning: Detectors are trained to model normal behavior without labeled attack data. Small variations in how "normal" is learned can dramatically affect what gets flagged as anomalous.

  2. Random initialization: Neural network weights are randomly initialized, leading to different optimization trajectories.

  3. Stochastic training: Mini-batch sampling, negative sampling, dropout, and other stochastic elements introduce variability between runs.

For example, on LANL, whether LARES selects the root attacker in the first stage of its evaluation depends on the seed and the epoch (see the header of config/lares.yml), and on OPTC_NET, label-free epoch selection picks a nearly arbitrary epoch (see Systems).

items.title: Measuring instability
items.text:
To quantify instability, PIDSMaker supports running a system multiple times and computing statistics across runs. Use the --experiment=run_n_times flag:

pidsmaker orthrus CADETS_E3 --wandb --background --experiment=run_n_times

This executes the pipeline N times using the same configuration, with each run using a different random seed.

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
Parameters are configured in config/experiments/uncertainty/run_n_times.yml:

training_loop:
  run_evaluation: each_epoch

experiment:
  used_method: uncertainty
  uncertainty:
    deep_ensemble:
      method: increasing_seed      # a new seed at each run
      iterations: 5                # number of runs
      restart_from: featurization  # task to restart from
Parameter Description method increasing_seed: run i uses the seed + i of the restart_from task, which must be featurization or training. same_seed: every run uses the same seed, so the variance only comes from non-deterministic operations. iterations Number of times to run the pipeline (default: 5) restart_from The pipeline stage to restart from for each iteration. Earlier stages (e.g., construction) are computed once and reused.

Any value can be overridden from the CLI, e.g. --experiment.uncertainty.deep_ensemble.iterations=10.

Tip

Setting restart_from: featurization or restart_from: training saves time by reusing graph construction and transformation outputs across runs. Set it to the earliest stage where randomness is introduced.

items.title: Reported metrics
items.text:
Upon completion, each metric is reported in three variants:

Suffix Description *_mean Mean value across all runs *_std Standard deviation across runs *_std_rel Relative standard deviation, in percent (100 × std / mean), useful for comparing instability across metrics with different scales

For example, if measuring precision score across 5 runs:

  • precision_mean: Average precision across runs
  • precision_std: Standard deviation of precision
  • precision_std_rel: Coefficient of variation, in percent (lower is more stable)

The metrics of the runs with the lowest and highest ADP are also logged with the _min and _max suffixes, the best run is logged under the plain metric names, and all runs are saved in uncertainty_exp/method_to_metrics.pkl in the evaluation folder.

items.title: Other experiments
items.text:
config/experiments/uncertainty/ provides other ways to perturb runs. Each key under experiment.uncertainty is a method, run one after the other:

Experiment Method What changes between runs run_n_times deep_ensemble The random seed (see above) run_n_times_hyperparameters hyperparameter Each hyperparameter of hyperparameters (lr, num_epochs, text_h_dim, gnn_h_dim) is moved by a relative step of ±delta, e.g. −40%, −20%, 0, +20%, +40% with 5 iterations (must be odd) uncertainty all four Runs hyperparameter, mc_dropout, deep_ensemble and bagged_ensemble in turn

mc_dropout adds dropout of rate dropout to every layer of the encoder and keeps it active at inference, so each run makes different predictions. bagged_ensemble is meant to train on a growing number of training days, starting at min_num_days.

pidsmaker orthrus CADETS_E3 --wandb --background --experiment=run_n_times_hyperparameters

To run a single method, write your own YAML in config/experiments/uncertainty/ and pass its name to --experiment. All arguments are listed in the Tasks reference.

Note

The framework is deterministic by default, instability appears when running multiple iterations within a same run (e.g., with run_n_times).

items.title: Reducing instability
items.text:
training.stable_optim: True trains the detector with an optimization setup designed to reduce the variance between runs:

  • AdamW (betas 0.9 and 0.99, weight decay 0.02) instead of Adam. training.weight_decay is then ignored.
  • Learning rate schedule: a linear warmup over the first 5% of the training steps, then a cosine decay down to 10% of training.lr.
  • Gradient clipping to a norm of 1.0.

It is off by default, and on in the pretrained encoder configs. It can be enabled for any system, for example with run_n_times to measure its effect on the *_std metrics:

pidsmaker orthrus CADETS_E3 --wandb --background --training.stable_optim=True --experiment=run_n_times

items.title: Recommendations
items.text:
Based on empirical observations:

  1. Run multiple times: We recommend running each configuration at least 3-5 times to get reliable performance estimates.

  2. Report ranges: When publishing results, report mean ± standard deviation rather than single-run numbers.

  3. Use the best run: For practical deployment, you may select the best-performing run from multiple attempts.

Warning

A single run with good metrics may not be reproducible. Always validate important results with multiple runs.

items.title: Multi-dataset training
items.text:
Train on the benign activity of several datasets, then evaluate on one of them. This tests whether a detector generalizes beyond the machine it was trained on, and gives it more benign data.

The dataset passed on the command line is the primary dataset: it is the only one evaluated. The others are listed in construction.multi_dataset, and two flags choose which stages learn from all of them:

Argument Effect construction.multi_dataset Comma-separated datasets to use besides the primary one (none by default). Their graphs are built and transformed. featurization.multi_dataset_training Trains the text embedding model on the labels of all the datasets. Only changes word2vec and fasttext. batching.multi_dataset_training Trains the detector on the training graphs of all the datasets, and validates on all their validation graphs.

For example, Orthrus trained on CADETS E3 and THEIA E3, and evaluated on CADETS E3:

pidsmaker orthrus CADETS_E3 \
  --construction.multi_dataset=CADETS_E3,THEIA_E3 \
  --featurization.multi_dataset_training=True \
  --batching.multi_dataset_training=True

Listing the primary dataset in multi_dataset is optional. Setting a multi_dataset_training flag without multi_dataset raises an error.

Provenance datasets

Multi-dataset training is designed for provenance datasets, and is not tested on network datasets. The other datasets are processed with the settings of the primary dataset, including its schema (node types, edge types and event attributes), so a provenance dataset and a network dataset can't be combined.

Mixing DARPA TC and OpTC

OpTC uses its own event types. With construction.consistent_edge_types: True, OpTC events are mapped to their DARPA TC equivalents (e.g. MESSAGE from a process to a network node becomes EVENT_SENDMSG), so that both share the same edge types. The pretrained encoder configs enable it.

items.title: Related: pretraining datasets
items.text:
Two other arguments train a featurization model on several datasets, without the rest of the pipeline:

  • featurization.pretrain_datasets: the datasets whose labels train word2vec. Their graphs must already have been built.
  • featurization.pretrained.pretrain_datasets: the datasets used to pretrain SPIDER and the other pretrained encoders.

items.title: Pretrained Encoders
items.text:
Most PIDSs turn the label of each entity (process command line, file path, IP address and port) into a vector with a model trained on the target dataset only, such as word2vec or doc2vec. PIDSMaker can instead use an encoder pretrained on provenance data: SPIDER, CyberGFM, masked language models, self-supervised GNNs, or general-purpose language models such as GPT-2 and Llama.

Provenance datasets

Pretrained encoders embed the textual labels of provenance entities, and are pretrained on provenance datasets. They are not tested on network datasets, whose hosts only have a name or an ID.

All pretrained encoders share one featurization method, featurization.used_method: pretrained, and featurization.pretrained.model_type picks the encoder. They can be used in two ways:

  • As a frozen featurizer (default): the encoder embeds the entities of the target dataset, and these embeddings become the node features of any PIDS. The detector itself is unchanged.
  • As a detector: the encoder is fine-tuned on the target dataset and scores edges directly, replacing the GNN.

items.title: Available encoders
items.text:
model_type Encoder spider SPIDER (NeurIPS 2026): a T5 encoder distilled from a GNN teacher. Pretrained weights available behavior_cluster, gnn_distill Earlier variants of SPIDER's distillation bert BERT trained with masked language modeling on random walks, as in CyberGFM roberta, modernbert, ropebert, logbert Variants of BERT: RoBERTa head, ModernBERT, RoPE, and LogBERT's hypersphere loss llama Decoder-only model trained from scratch with next-token prediction on random walks gpt2_pretrained GPT-2 (model_size: small, medium, large or xl), fine-tuned on entity labels llama3_pretrained Llama 3.2 (model_size: 1b or 3b), fine-tuned on entity labels. Requires huggingface-cli login, since Llama is gated opt_pretrained OPT-1.3B, fine-tuned on entity labels deepwalk, node2vec Word2Vec on random walks over entity labels (no transformer) graphmae, gae, dgi Self-supervised GNNs: masked feature reconstruction, link prediction and mutual information

config/pretrained/README.md describes each encoder and its options, and config/pretrained/pretrained.yml lists all options with their default values.

items.title: Using an encoder in a PIDS
items.text:
One config is provided per PIDS. Each one includes the PIDS config and pretrained.yml, so the detector stays the same and only its node features change.

Config PIDS pretrained_velox Velox pretrained_orthrus Orthrus pretrained_kairos Kairos pretrained_magic MAGIC pretrained_flash Flash pretrained_nodlink NodLink pretrained_threatrace ThreaTrace

They use SPIDER by default. Set featurization.pretrained.model_type to use another encoder, for example GPT-2 or DeepWalk in Velox:

pidsmaker pretrained_velox CADETS_E3 --featurization.pretrained.model_type=gpt2_pretrained --featurization.pretrained.model_size=small --featurization.tokenization.used_method=huggingface
pidsmaker pretrained_velox CADETS_E3 --featurization.pretrained.model_type=deepwalk --featurization.tokenization.used_method=whole_label

These configs also enable training.stable_optim.

items.title: Pretraining
items.text:
Without pretrained weights, the encoder is first pretrained on the benign data of the datasets listed in featurization.pretrained.pretrain_datasets: by default PROVENANCE_BENIGN, TRACE_E3, TRACE_E5, CADETS_E5, CLEARSCOPE_E3 and optc_h201. Each of them must be installed as a database. PROVENANCE_BENIGN is a Linux audit corpus that contains only benign activity (see Datasets).

The trained encoder is saved in the stored_models/ folder of the run's featurization artifacts. Pass that folder with --featurization.pretrained.weights_path to reuse it in other runs without pretraining again. The path must be absolute, because its files are symlinked into each run's artifact folder.

The main options are:

  • featurization.pretrained.model_size: tiny, mini, med or baseline for the encoders trained from scratch, or the variant of GPT-2, Llama and OPT.
  • featurization.pretrained.training: token budget (pretrain_tokens, warmup_tokens), batch_size and lr.
  • featurization.tokenization: bpe (vocabulary size, maximum label length and substitutions of hashes, UUIDs, IPs, ports, …) for most encoders, whole_label for DeepWalk and Node2Vec, huggingface for GPT-2, Llama and OPT (see Tokenization).
  • featurization.pretrained.walks: random walks used by the masked language models and DeepWalk.

All options are listed in the featurization arguments.

items.title: SPIDER
items.text: SPIDER (NeurIPS 2026) is our pretrained entity encoder. During pretraining, a GNN teacher learns an embedding of each entity from its neighborhood in the graph, and a small T5 encoder is distilled to predict the teacher's embedding from the entity's label alone. At detection time, only the T5 encoder is used, so it embeds entities from their label only, including entities never seen during pretraining.

items.title: Pretrained weights
items.text:
Download the weights used in the paper (Google Drive, 21 MB), e.g. with gdown (pip install gdown):

gdown 1NlUPQJTEehhe3cAOjlOq_wnPYjV-MMZ9 -O SPIDER-weights.tar.gz
mkdir -p weights && tar -xzf SPIDER-weights.tar.gz -C weights
(cd weights/spider && sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS)

Then pass the path of the folder (below, $PWD/weights/spider: the weights downloaded in the current folder) to any pretrained_<pids> config:

pidsmaker pretrained_velox CADETS_E3 --featurization.pretrained.weights_path=$PWD/weights/spider

The folder contains:

File Content pretrain_mini.pt T5 encoder (model_size: mini) tokenizer.pt BPE tokenizer of entity labels gnn_teacher_mini_best.pt GNN teacher, only needed to continue pretraining behavior_vocab.txt, edge_type2idx.json Behavior labels and edge types of the teacher, only needed to continue pretraining spider_log_mini.txt Pretraining loss log

items.title: Continued pretraining on the target dataset
items.text:
With feat_inference.continue_pretrain: True, SPIDER is further pretrained on the benign training data of the target dataset before embedding its entities. This needs the teacher files of the weights folder. feat_inference.continue_pretrain_epochs (10 in pretrained.yml) and feat_inference.continue_pretrain_lr_factor (0.1, relative to the pretraining learning rate) control this step.

pidsmaker pretrained_velox CADETS_E3 --featurization.pretrained.weights_path=$PWD/weights/spider --feat_inference.continue_pretrain=True

items.title: Renaming attack
items.text:
feat_inference.rename_attack evaluates robustness to an attacker who renames malicious processes to benign names. At inference, the test-set entities whose label matches one of entities (exact match, or path ending with /<entity>) get the embedding of a benign name instead. The benign name is either drawn from the top_k most frequent labels of the training set, or fixed with target_label (when top_k: 0).

For example, on CADETS_E3, renaming its attack processes to frequent benign names:

pidsmaker pretrained_velox CADETS_E3 --featurization.pretrained.weights_path=$PWD/weights/spider \
    --feat_inference.rename_attack.enabled=True \
    --feat_inference.rename_attack.entities="main, pEja72mA, XIM, tmux-1002, font, sendmail" \
    --feat_inference.rename_attack.target_node_type=subject \
    --feat_inference.rename_attack.top_k=100

items.title: Checkpoint selection
items.text: During pretraining, spider and behavior_cluster are evaluated after each epoch on the 528 labeled entities of config/eval/eval_set_clustering.json: a k-nearest-neighbors classifier must recover the role of each entity (browser, database, crypto, …) from its embedding. The checkpoint with the best accuracy is kept (pretrain_<size>_best.pt, and gnn_teacher_<size>_best.pt for SPIDER's teacher), and it is the one used at inference. The other encoders keep their last checkpoint.

items.title: Reproducing the paper
items.text:
The spider branch contains the exact code used for the paper, and its README lists the commands of every experiment. With this version, the Velox results of the paper are reproduced by the commands below, after downloading the weights. --experiment=run_n_times trains 5 seeds and logs the mean and standard deviation to W&B (without --wandb, they are printed in the logs). Results can differ slightly from the paper because of newer library versions.

ARGS="--experiment=run_n_times --featurization.pretrained.weights_path=$PWD/weights/spider"

# Frozen encoder
pidsmaker pretrained_velox CADETS_E3 --wandb --background $ARGS --training.num_epochs=22
pidsmaker pretrained_velox THEIA_E3 --wandb --background $ARGS
pidsmaker pretrained_velox THEIA_E5 --wandb --background $ARGS
pidsmaker pretrained_velox CLEARSCOPE_E5 --wandb --background $ARGS --training.node_hid_dim=128 --training.node_out_dim=128
pidsmaker pretrained_velox optc_h051 --wandb --background $ARGS --training.node_hid_dim=256 --training.node_out_dim=256

# Continued pretraining (fine-tuned SPIDER in the paper)
pidsmaker pretrained_velox CADETS_E3 --wandb --background $ARGS --feat_inference.continue_pretrain=True --feat_inference.continue_pretrain_epochs=10
pidsmaker pretrained_velox THEIA_E3 --wandb --background $ARGS --feat_inference.continue_pretrain=True --feat_inference.continue_pretrain_epochs=10
pidsmaker pretrained_velox THEIA_E5 --wandb --background $ARGS --feat_inference.continue_pretrain=True --feat_inference.continue_pretrain_epochs=5
pidsmaker pretrained_velox CLEARSCOPE_E5 --wandb --background $ARGS --feat_inference.continue_pretrain=True --feat_inference.continue_pretrain_epochs=1
pidsmaker pretrained_velox optc_h051 --wandb --background $ARGS --feat_inference.continue_pretrain=True --feat_inference.continue_pretrain_epochs=10

items.title: Fine-tuning the encoder as a detector
items.text:
With training.used_method: pretrained, the GNN detector is bypassed: the pretrained encoder is fine-tuned on the target dataset and scores edges directly. training.pretrained.finetune_mode picks the fine-tuning objective:

finetune_mode Objective lp Link prediction: an edge's score is its reconstruction error mlm Masked-token reconstruction of the walks around an edge cls Ranking benign walks against perturbed ones (no labels) cls_attack Classification with walks from ground-truth attack edges (supervised) edge_cls Edge type classification from the endpoint embeddings tgn A TGN trained on top of the frozen embeddings (options under training.pretrained.tgn) perplexity No fine-tuning: next-token perplexity of a causal model (model_type: llama)

config/pretrained/cybergfm/cybergfm.yml implements the CyberGFM baseline this way, with BERT pretraining followed by link prediction:

pidsmaker cybergfm CADETS_E3

items.title: Supervised Fine-Tuning with Attack Edges
items.text: PIDSs, like the network systems, usually learn from benign data only. The predict_edge_supervised objective adds some supervision: a binary classifier learns to separate the benign edges of the training graphs from a set of attack edges that you provide, then scores every test edge by how much it looks like an attack.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
• Input: for each edge, the decoder receives the source and destination node features, each concatenated with the one-hot edge type. The GNN encoder is bypassed, so the node features themselves must be informative: this objective is meant to be used with pretrained encoder embeddings, such as SPIDER.
  • Training: the negatives are the edges of the training graphs. The attack edges are the positives, oversampled with replacement to match each batch of benign edges. pos_weight adds weight to the attack class in the binary cross-entropy loss.
  • Detection: the anomaly score of a test edge is its loss against the benign label, which grows with the predicted probability of being an attack.

The attack edges are described with provenance entities and event types, and config/attack_edges/ only covers DARPA TC datasets: this objective is not tested on network datasets.

Enable it by setting the objective in the training.decoder section:

training:
  decoder:
    used_methods: predict_edge_supervised
    predict_edge_supervised:
      mode: synthetic
      attack_edges_path: config/attack_edges/cadets_e3.yml
      pos_weight: 1.0
      decoder: edge_mlp
      edge_mlp:
        architecture_str: linear(0.5) | relu
        src_dst_projection_coef: 2

items.title: Attack edges from a YAML file (mode: synthetic)
items.text:
In this mode, the attack edges are written by hand in a YAML file and don't need to exist in the dataset. During the feat_inference task, SPIDER embeds the labels of their nodes, so this mode requires featurization.used_method: pretrained.

Each edge gives the type and label of its two nodes and the event type:

attack_edges:
  # nginx (exploited web server) spawns a shell
  - src_type: subject
    src_label: "subject None nginx"
    edge_type: EVENT_CLONE
    dst_type: subject
    dst_label: "subject None sh"

Labels follow the format of the dataset's node labels, set by construction.node_label_features: with the default subject: type, path, cmd_line, a process label is subject <path> <command line>, and None stands for a missing attribute.

config/attack_edges/ provides one file for CADETS_E3, CADETS_E5, THEIA_E3, THEIA_E5, TRACE_E3 and TRACE_E5. Each file describes an attack similar to the dataset's scenario, but with different indicators (such as C2 IP addresses), so that the classifier can't simply memorize the real attack.

pretrained_supervised.yml runs Velox with SPIDER embeddings and this objective on CADETS_E3:

pidsmaker pretrained_supervised CADETS_E3 --featurization.pretrained.weights_path=$PWD/weights/spider

Note

The attack labels are embedded when the feat_inference task runs. If that task already ran with the same settings, for example with pretrained_velox, it is skipped and the embeddings are missing: add --force_restart=feat_inference.

For another dataset, point attack_edges_path to its file:

pidsmaker pretrained_supervised THEIA_E3 --featurization.pretrained.weights_path=$PWD/weights/spider \
    --training.decoder.predict_edge_supervised.attack_edges_path=config/attack_edges/theia_e3.yml

items.title: Attack edges matched in the data (mode: patterns)
items.text:
In this mode, the attack edges are collected from the validation and test graphs with a list of patterns. Each pattern can set any of src_type, src_label_contains, dst_type, dst_label_contains and edge_type; a missing field matches anything. max_edges_per_pattern caps the number of edges collected per pattern.

training:
  decoder:
    used_methods: predict_edge_supervised
    predict_edge_supervised:
      mode: patterns
      max_edges_per_pattern: 50
      attack_patterns:
        - src_type: subject
          src_label_contains: nginx
          edge_type: EVENT_CLONE

Warning

In this mode the positives come from the evaluation data, so the results are not comparable with those of unsupervised PIDSs.

All options are listed in the objective arguments.

items.title: Triage
items.text:
Detection flags individual nodes, but an analyst needs to know how an attack unfolded. Triage, the last stage of the pipeline, starts from the detected nodes and reconstructs the attack around them, which can also discard isolated false positives.

Two methods are available, selected with triage.used_method:

Method Idea Works with depimpact Traces the dependencies of each detected node backward to its entry points and forward to its exit points, and keeps the most suspicious paths node_evaluation, node_tw_evaluation ocrapt_subgraph Groups detected nodes into connected subgraphs around the most anomalous seeds, and keeps the most severe subgraphs node_evaluation

Triage starts from node-level detections: it applies to provenance systems, and to any system evaluated with node_evaluation (or node_tw_evaluation for DepImpact). The edge-level and host-centered evaluations of network systems are not triaged. OCR-APT runs with its subgraph triage on LANL in the tests (tests/test_network_datasets.py); DepImpact, which traces causal dependencies in provenance graphs, is not tested on network datasets.

Triage is off by default in every system except OCR-APT. Its arguments have no default values: when you enable a method, set all of its arguments, on the CLI or in the YAML config. Triage only runs after evaluation, and changing its arguments re-runs triage alone (see Caching of tasks).

flowchart LR
    A["Evaluation<br/>detected nodes + scores"] --> B{triage.used_method}
    B -- depimpact --> C["Backward and forward<br/>dependency tracing"]
    B -- ocrapt_subgraph --> D["Anomalous subgraph<br/>construction"]
    C --> E["New predictions<br/>tracing_* metrics"]
    D --> E
    classDef stage fill:#e5602a1f,stroke:#e5602a,stroke-width:1.5px;
    class A,C,D,E stage;

items.title: DepImpact
items.text:
Each node flagged as malicious is a point of interest (POI), processed in its time-window graph.

  1. Scoring. Every node of the graph gets a score, set by score_method: degree (out-degree divided by in-degree), recon_loss (its anomaly score from evaluation), or degree_recon (the sum of both, min-max normalized).
  2. Dependency graph. The time-window graph is turned into a DAG ordered by time: a node that receives a new edge gets a new version, so that paths always move forward in time.
  3. Backward tracing. From the POI to the entry points of the DAG (nodes without incoming edges). Each entry point is scored by the mean score of the nodes between it and the POI, and the best-scored entries are kept.
  4. Forward tracing. The same, from the POI to the exit points (nodes without outgoing edges).
  5. New predictions. All nodes of the kept paths are predicted malicious, and the metrics are recomputed.

used_method sets how the nodes between an entry (or exit) point and the POI are collected:

triage.depimpact.used_method Nodes kept component All nodes on any path between the entry/exit point and the POI shortest_path Only the nodes of the shortest path 1-hop, 2-hop, 3-hop No tracing: the undirected n-hop neighborhood of the POI 
pidsmaker velox CADETS_E3 \
  --triage.used_method=depimpact \
  --triage.depimpact.used_method=component \
  --triage.depimpact.score_method=degree \
  --triage.depimpact.workers=8

workers is the number of processes that trace POIs in parallel. With --triage.depimpact.visualize=True, an image of the reconstructed attack graph is saved for each time window.

Known issues

In the current version, score_method=recon_loss gives every node a score of 0 (so degree_recon behaves like degree), and forward tracing with used_method=shortest_path finds no path. Use component with degree.

items.title: OCR-APT subgraphs
items.text:
This method follows the anomalous subgraph construction of OCR-APT (Section 5.2, Algorithm 1). It is enabled by default in the ocrapt system.

  1. Normalized scores. The anomaly score of each detected node is normalized to [0, 1] with the range of training losses of its node type.
  2. Seeds. For each node type, the top_k detected nodes with the highest scores are used as seeds, most anomalous first.
  3. Expansion. Each seed is grown with its anomalous neighbors, and, if num_hops ≥ 1, with the anomalous neighbors of its neighbors. With correlate_anomalous_once, a node joins at most one subgraph. Subgraphs smaller than min_nodes are dropped.
  4. Splitting. Subgraphs with more than max_edges edges are split into Louvain communities and sampled per edge type (max_edges: 0 disables this).
  5. Severity. The severity of a subgraph is the sum of the normalized scores of its anomalous nodes: Negligible (≤ 1), Minor (≤ 10), Moderate (≤ 100), Significant (≤ 1000) or Critical. Only subgraphs at or above abnormality_level are kept, and duplicates are removed with remove_duplicated_subgraph.

The nodes of the kept subgraphs become the new predictions. As in OCR-APT, the metrics are computed with a 2-hop tolerance: a false positive within 2 hops of an attack node is not counted, and an attack node within 2 hops of a true positive counts as detected.

pidsmaker orthrus CADETS_E3 \
  --triage.used_method=ocrapt_subgraph \
  --triage.ocrapt.num_hops=1 --triage.ocrapt.top_k=15 \
  --triage.ocrapt.min_nodes=3 --triage.ocrapt.max_edges=5000 \
  --triage.ocrapt.abnormality_level=Negligible \
  --triage.ocrapt.correlate_anomalous_once=True \
  --triage.ocrapt.remove_duplicated_subgraph=True

Note

The score normalization needs the training losses, which are only computed when training.ocrapt_early_stop.enabled=True, as in the ocrapt config. Without them, every subgraph is Negligible: use abnormality_level=Negligible on other systems.

items.title: Results
items.text:
Triage results are logged with a tracing_ prefix (e.g. tracing_precision, tracing_recall), next to the metrics of evaluation, which are left unchanged.

  • DepImpact recomputes all metrics with the new predictions; ap and auc don't change, since the scores are the same. Its results are saved in the tracing_graphs/ folder of the triage task: a CSV with, for each POI, the number of true and false positives reached, and the traced subgraphs.
  • OCR-APT logs the precision, recall, F-score, TP, FP, FN and the number of subgraphs kept.

Both methods use the epoch with the best MCC. All arguments are listed in the Tasks reference.

items.title: Hyperparameter Tuning
items.text: PIDSMaker simplifies hyperparameter tuning by combining its efficient pipeline design with the power of W&B Sweeps.

items.title: Dataset-specific tuning
items.text:
Tuning is configured using YAML files, just like system definitions. For example, suppose you've created a new system named my_system, and its configuration is stored in config/my_system.yml. To search for optimal hyperparameters on the THEIA_E3 dataset, you can create a new tuning configuration file at config/experiments/tuning/systems/theia_e3/tuning_my_system.yml following the W&B syntax:

tuning_my_system.yml
method: grid # (1)!

parameters:
  training.lr:
    values: [0.001, 0.0001]
  training.node_hid_dim:
    values: [32, 64, 128, 256]
  featurization.used_method:
    values: [fasttext, word2vec]
  1. Other hyperparameter search strategies like random and bayesian can be used (more info here).

Before starting the hyperparameter search, make sure you are logged in to W&B by running wandb login. Then, launch the hyperparameter tuning with --tuning_mode=hyperparameters:

pidsmaker my_system THEIA_E3 --wandb --background --tuning_mode=hyperparameters

This flag will automatically load the tuning configuration from config/experiments/tuning/systems/theia_e3/tuning_my_system.yml, based on the provided dataset and system names. Any overlapping arguments defined in config/my_system.yml will be overridden by those specified in the tuning file. If the specified tuning file does not exist (i.e., no dataset-specific configuration is available), the pipeline falls back to the default tuning configuration: config/experiments/tuning/systems/default/tuning_default_baselines.yml.

Note

You can also pass arguments directly via the CLI. CLI arguments always take precedence and will override both the system configuration (config/my_system.yml) and the tuning configuration (tuning_my_system.yml).

items.title: Cross-dataset tuning
items.text:
If you wish to use the same hyperparameter tuning configuration across all datasets, you can explicitly specify the tuning file as a command-line argument. For instance, you might create a tuning file named config/experiments/tuning/systems/default/tuning_my_system_all_datasets.yml, then apply it to all dataset by running:

for dataset in CLEARSCOPE_E3 CADETS_E3 THEIA_E3 CLEARSCOPE_E5 THEIA_E5 CADETS_E5; do
    pidsmaker my_system $dataset --wandb --restart_from_scratch \
        --tuning_mode=hyperparameters \
        --tuning_file_path=systems/default/tuning_my_system_all_datasets
done

or on a single dataset:

pidsmaker my_system CLEARSCOPE_E3 --wandb --background \
    --tuning_mode=hyperparameters \
    --tuning_file_path=systems/default/tuning_my_system_all_datasets

The path passed to --tuning_file_path should start from systems/.

Tip

For a better historization of experiments, we recommend to assign a name to each sweep (--exp) and a dedicated project name (--project):

pidsmaker my_system CADETS_E3 --wandb --background \
    --tuning_mode=hyperparameters \
    --exp=bench_fasttext_word2vec \
    --project=best_featurization_method

items.title: Best model selection
items.text:
Once the sweep has finished, the best run can be obtained from W&B by sorting based on your desired metric.

Get the hyperparameters associated with the best run and put them into a config/tuned_baselines/{dataset}/tuned_my_system.yml.

tuned_my_system.yml
featurization:
  used_method: word2vec

training:
  lr: 0.0001
  node_hid_dim: 128

Each system should have a tuned file per dataset, or the best hyperparameters can be directly set in its my_system.yml file if it uses the same hyperparameters in all datasets.

Note

The process of best hyperparameter selection is currently done by hand but will likely be automated in future.

items.title: Run a tuned system
items.text:
Running a system with its best hyperparameters on a particular dataset is as simple as adding --tuned:

pidsmaker my_system CADETS_E3 --wandb --background --tuned

This will search for the config/tuned_baselines/cadets_e3/tuned_my_system.yml file and override the default system config by the best hyperparameters.

For example, the defaults of the network systems are those of LANL, and config/tuned_baselines/optc_net/ holds the OpTC settings of LARES and Argus:

pidsmaker lares OPTC_NET --tuned

items.title: Embedding Visualizer
items.text:
PIDSMaker ships an interactive 3D web viewer for exploring a run's node embeddings in the browser. A Flask server reads the artifacts a run already produced and serves a Three.js front end; it is independent of the pipeline — you generate the data for a run, then open it in the viewer.

It renders the per-node embeddings (UMAP or t-SNE projection) and supports:

  • Temporal playback — points appear and fade with their time window.
  • Per-node inspection — click a node for its path, type, label, anomaly score, and a K-nearest-neighbour analysis; extract its causal subgraph or incident edges.
  • Two embedding spaces — switch between the featurization space and the GNN encoder space, with an epoch selector for the encoder.
  • Overlays — temporal trajectories, the attack graph, a discrimination heatmap, and false-positive highlighting.

Provenance runs

The viewer colors nodes by provenance type (process, file, netflow). It is not tested on the runs of network datasets.

items.title: Running the viewer
items.text:
Start the server where PIDSMaker is installed. The UMAP projection needs the viz extra (pip install "pidsmaker[viz]").

python -m pidsmaker.vizgen.web.viz_server

The server lists the runs of the artifact folder: $PIDS_ARTIFACTS_DIR if it is set, else the default of --artifact_dir (see Where files are stored).

Then open http://127.0.0.1:5000. The last run you viewed loads automatically; use Open Run Browser (top of the left panel) to pick another. When viewing from another machine, tunnel over SSH (ssh -N -L 5000:localhost:5000 <user>@<server>).

Tip

If localhost is refused but 127.0.0.1 works, the server is bound to IPv4 only (--host 0.0.0.0) while localhost resolves to IPv6; start it with --host :: to serve both.

items.title: Generating viz data for a run
items.text:
A run needs an embedding export before it can be opened. The easiest path is the in-browser Run Browser → Generate button; you can also generate from the CLI:

python -m pidsmaker.vizgen.web.export SYSTEM DATASET --embeddings both

items.title: Opt in when training: --save_for_viz
items.text:
Generation is fastest and most complete when the training run pre-saved the extra artifacts the exporter reuses — the per-epoch model checkpoints (for the GNN-encoder space and epoch selector) and a cached copy of the test graphs. These are large and most runs never open the viewer, so they are off by default and enabled per run:

pidsmaker SYSTEM DATASET --save_for_viz

Enable it on the runs you intend to explore. Without it, a run is still discoverable and you can still generate viz data, but the featurization space works normally while the GNN encoder space needs the checkpoints (skipped with a warning if absent), and the test graphs are recomputed on demand.

items.title: More details
items.text: The web viewer has its own README covering the run browser, generation options, buffer/streaming design, and endpoints: pidsmaker/vizgen/web/README.md.

items.title: Building datasets from scratch
items.text:
PIDSMaker downloads preprocessed versions of all its datasets. This guide builds them yourself, for instance to change the parsing: the provenance datasets from the official DARPA files, and the network datasets (LANL and the network flows of OpTC) from the preprocessed files of LARES. The scripts write Parquet datasets with the tables and columns of the downloaded ones, without any database server.

Plan for time and disk space

Downloading, uncompressing and parsing raw files takes hours and a lot of storage, especially for E5 datasets and OpTC flows: the raw files take much more space than the datasets, and the scripts write temporary files (unsorted events) about as large as the dataset. The events are sorted with DuckDB, which uses up to 80% of the RAM and spills the rest to disk (about 85 GB of RAM for the 1.9 billion events of optc_net, built in 42 minutes). Running experiments takes more: a single run can produce more than 15 GB of artifacts on E3 datasets, and much more on E5.

The node tables of a dataset built from scratch are in the order in which the scripts write them, which can differ from the order of the downloaded datasets: features, which depend on this order, can differ slightly from those of the downloaded dataset.

The scripts are in the repository: install PIDSMaker from source (pip install -e .) and run them from its root.

Both kinds of datasets follow the same five steps. Pick your dataset in the tabs of each step.

items.title: 1. Download the raw files
items.text:
Create an empty folder for the raw data:

DATA_FOLDER=./data
mkdir ${DATA_FOLDER}
pip install gdown

Note

DATA_FOLDER must be empty before downloading and parsing a dataset. Remove the files of a previous dataset first.

DARPA TC (E3, E5)DARPA OpTCNetwork (LANL, OpTC flows) 
./dataset_preprocessing/darpa_tc/scripts/download_DATASET.sh ${DATA_FOLDER}

DATASET is one of clearscope_e3, cadets_e3, theia_e3, clearscope_e5, cadets_e5 or theia_e5, and DATA_FOLDER is the absolute path of the output folder. The datasets built in step 4 are CADETS_E3, THEIA_E3, CADETS_E5 and THEIA_E5, whose files are listed in dataset_preprocessing/darpa_tc/filelist.py.

python ./dataset_preprocessing/optc/download_dataset.py DATASET ${DATA_FOLDER}

DATASET is one of optc_h051, optc_h201 or optc_h501, and DATA_FOLDER is the absolute path of the output folder.

Download the archive of LARES, with the preprocessed files and labels of both datasets (14.35 GB, 18.44 GB once extracted):

curl -L -o ${DATA_FOLDER}/lanl_optc_datasets.tar.gz "https://drive.usercontent.google.com/download?id=10fdDttLXP8zYwlrhqFzOe_kEvDGokfVY&export=download&confirm=t"

items.title: Downloading the files manually
items.text:
For DARPA TC, you can also pick the files by hand on Google Drive. All files go in DATA_FOLDER:

  1. Data: all the .gz files of the dataset, from the E3 or E5 folder.
  2. Java consumer: ta3-java-consumer.tar.gz, which converts the Avro files, for E3 or E5.
  3. Schema: the .avdl and .avsc files, for E3 or E5.

From the command line, use gdown with the ID of each file, taken from its URL. If a download stops, press Ctrl+C and re-run the same command with --continue.

For the network datasets, LANL can also be built from its official files, requested on the LANL website (authentications only, see step 4), and the official network flows of OpTC (ecar-bro folder of its Google Drive) are downloaded with:

python dataset_preprocessing/optc/download_optc_net.py ${DATA_FOLDER}/optc_net

items.title: 2. Get Java for DARPA TC
items.text:
The raw files of DARPA TC are Avro files, converted to JSON by the Java consumer of DARPA, which needs Java 8 and Maven. Install them in your conda environment, or with the package manager of your system (e.g. sudo apt install openjdk-8-jdk maven):

conda install -c conda-forge openjdk=8 maven

The other datasets need nothing more than PIDSMaker.

items.title: 3. Extract the files
items.text:
DARPA TC (E3, E5)DARPA OpTCNetwork (LANL, OpTC flows) 
./dataset_preprocessing/darpa_tc/scripts/uncompress_darpa_files.sh ${DATA_FOLDER}/

This may take several hours, depending on the dataset.

./dataset_preprocessing/optc/extract_data.sh ${DATA_FOLDER}/

tar -xzf ${DATA_FOLDER}/lanl_optc_datasets.tar.gz -C ${DATA_FOLDER}/

items.title: 4. Build the dataset
items.text:
Each script writes a dataset to <datasets_dir>/<database>/, where PIDSMaker reads it: --datasets_dir, else $PIDSMAKER_DATASETS_DIR, else ~/.cache/pidsmaker/datasets (see Where files are stored), and the database of the dataset, e.g. cadets_e3. The dataset is written to <database>.tmp and renamed once complete. An existing dataset, e.g. a downloaded one, is only replaced with --overwrite.

DARPA TC E3DARPA TC E5DARPA OpTCLANLOpTC flows 
python dataset_preprocessing/darpa_tc/create_database_e3.py orthrus DATASET --raw_dir ${DATA_FOLDER}

DATASET is CADETS_E3 or THEIA_E3.

python dataset_preprocessing/darpa_tc/create_database_e5.py orthrus DATASET --raw_dir ${DATA_FOLDER}

DATASET is CADETS_E5 or THEIA_E5.

python dataset_preprocessing/optc/create_database_optc.py orthrus DATASET --raw_dir ${DATA_FOLDER}

DATASET is one of optc_h051, optc_h201 or optc_h501.

python dataset_preprocessing/lanl/create_database_lanl.py LANL --lares_dir ${DATA_FOLDER}/lanl_optc_datasets/LANL/preprocessed

This builds the lanl dataset with the NTLM authentications of the LANL "Comprehensive, Multi-Source Cyber-Security Events" dataset, as used by Euler, Argus, Jbeil and LARES. Add --with_flows to also load its network flows.

From the official files of LANL instead (authentications only):

python dataset_preprocessing/lanl/create_database_lanl.py LANL --auth_file ${DATA_FOLDER}/auth.txt.gz --redteam_file ${DATA_FOLDER}/redteam.txt.gz

LANL timestamps are seconds from an undisclosed origin. They are mapped to UTC dates such that the first red team event happens on 2015-01-03: by default, models are trained on 2015-01-01, validated on 2015-01-02 and tested from 2015-01-03 to 2015-01-30.

python dataset_preprocessing/optc/create_database_optc_net.py OPTC_NET --lares_dir ${DATA_FOLDER}/lanl_optc_datasets/OPTC/preprocessed

This builds the optc_net dataset with the FLOW START and FLOW MESSAGE events of all the hosts of DARPA OpTC (about 1.9 billion events). Files are read by --num_workers processes (16 by default), each writing its events to temporary files, which are then sorted into the dataset. As in LARES and Argus, graphs are built from FLOW START events only: set construction.operations=all to also use FLOW MESSAGE events, or a comma-separated list of operations (e.g. construction.operations=FLOW_START) to select events of any dataset.

Labels. A flow is recorded several times in OpTC (FLOW START and FLOW MESSAGE events, by the hosts at both ends), and LARES labels only some of these records: e.g. in the lateral movement of 2019-09-24, the FLOW MESSAGE events of 561 flows are malicious but the FLOW START of only 56 of them. By default, the script labels malicious all the records of a malicious flow (same 5-tuple, in either direction, in the same LARES file): 5,165 malicious events (1,015 FLOW START) instead of 2,370 (115 FLOW START). Add --no_label_propagation to keep the labels of LARES as they are. A dataset built without propagation can be relabelled in place with --relabel; graphs built before must then be built again (the labels of edges are stored in the graphs).

items.title: 5. Check the result
items.text:
Run a system on the new dataset:

ProvenanceNetwork 
pidsmaker orthrus DATASET

pidsmaker euler LANL

items.title: Sharing a dataset
items.text:
A dataset is a folder, <datasets_dir>/<database>/, with a manifest.json and the Parquet files of its tables: copy the folder to share it. To publish it on Hugging Face, as the datasets of PIDSMaker, upload the folder to a dataset repository (hf upload-large-folder REPO <folder> --repo-type dataset, with one folder per database at the root of the repository), and download it with pidsmaker download DATASET --repo REPO.

Adding a new dataset

To add a dataset that PIDSMaker does not support yet, provenance or network, see Adding custom datasets.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
A few minutes from a fresh machine to your first run. PIDSMaker is a Python package: install it with pip, download a dataset, and run a system. Datasets are Parquet files that PIDSMaker reads in place with DuckDB: nothing else to set up.

Requirements

  • Linux, ideally with an NVIDIA NVIDIA GPU, for all datasets. Without a GPU, PIDSMaker falls back to CPU.
  • macOS (Apple Silicon), on CPU, for most datasets: 32 GB of RAM is ideal. See macOS.
  • Python 3.9 to 3.11: PyTorch 2.1.2, which PIDSMaker pins, has no wheels for Python 3.12 and later. We create the environment with conda.
  • Disk space for the datasets you pick (see the table below) and for the artifacts of your runs (a single run can produce 15 GB or more on E3 datasets).

On an HPC cluster, see HPC clusters.

items.title: 1. Install PIDSMaker
items.text:
From PyPIFrom source 
conda create -n pids python=3.11
conda activate pids
pip install pidsmaker

To change the code or the configs of PIDSMaker, e.g. to add a system, install it from a clone of the repository, in editable mode: your changes are used without reinstalling.

git clone https://github.com/ubc-provenance/PIDSMaker.git && cd PIDSMaker
conda create -n pids python=3.11
conda activate pids
pip install -e .

This installs the pidsmaker command, with the configs of all systems and the ground truth of all datasets. Check it with pidsmaker --help.

PyTorch with CUDA, or CPU only

PIDSMaker pins torch==2.1.2. On Linux, pip installs it from PyPI with CUDA 12.1, which runs on an NVIDIA GPU when there is one, and on CPU otherwise. On a machine without a GPU, you can install the much smaller CPU-only build of PyTorch first:

pip install torch==2.1.2 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
pip install pidsmaker
Optional: compiled extensions of PyTorch Geometric

PIDSMaker does not need the compiled extensions of PyTorch Geometric (pyg_lib, torch_scatter, torch_sparse...): without them, it falls back to pure PyTorch, with the same results. With an NVIDIA GPU, you can install them for CUDA 12.1:

pip install pyg_lib torch_scatter torch_sparse torch_cluster torch_spline_conv -f https://data.pyg.org/whl/torch-2.1.0+cu121.html

Optional dependencies are installed as extras, e.g. pip install "pidsmaker[viz]", or pip install -e ".[viz,test]" from source:

Extra Installs For viz umap-learn The UMAP projections of the embedding visualizer test pytest, pytest-xdist... The tests

items.title: 2. Download the datasets
items.text:
DARPA TC and OpTC are very large and hard to process: we provide preprocessed versions of all the datasets, as Parquet files in the Hugging Face repository pidsmaker/datasets. The network datasets are built from the preprocessed files of LARES.

Dataset Family Size (GB) CADETS_E3 Provenance 1.3 THEIA_E3 Provenance 0.71 CLEARSCOPE_E3 Provenance 0.51 FIVEDIRECTIONS_E3 Provenance 2.3 TRACE_E3 Provenance 9.4 CADETS_E5 Provenance 32.9 THEIA_E5 Provenance 3.9 CLEARSCOPE_E5 Provenance 5.0 FIVEDIRECTIONS_E5 Provenance 30.3 TRACE_E5 Provenance 74.3 optc_h201 Provenance 1.6 optc_h501 Provenance 1.2 optc_h051 Provenance 1.3 ATLASV2_EDR Provenance 0.16 CARBANAKV2_EDR Provenance 1.1 LANL Network 0.40 OPTC_NET Network 11.8

Datasets keep this size when they are used: DuckDB reads the files in place, nothing is loaded into a database. (PIDSMaker 4.x read its datasets from a Postgres server, with Docker: it stays available at the tag 4.0.0.) PROVENANCE_BENIGN (2 MB), the corpus used to pretrain SPIDER, is downloaded the same way.

New to PIDSMaker?

Start with CADETS_E3, THEIA_E3 or CLEARSCOPE_E3 for provenance-based detection, and LANL for network detection: they are small, quick to download, and the most widely used in papers.

Download one or more datasets by name (case-insensitive):

pidsmaker download CADETS_E3 LANL   # some datasets
pidsmaker download all              # all datasets (about 180 GB)
pidsmaker download --list           # the datasets, their sizes, and which are downloaded

Datasets are stored in ~/.cache/pidsmaker/datasets/, one folder per dataset. To store them elsewhere, e.g. on a larger disk, set PIDSMAKER_DATASETS_DIR (e.g. in your ~/.bashrc), or pass --datasets_dir to both pidsmaker download and your runs. Interrupted downloads resume where they stopped when you run the command again, and datasets already downloaded are skipped (--force downloads them again). The other options are listed in the command line reference.

You can also skip this step: a run downloads its dataset the first time it needs it (set PIDSMAKER_AUTO_DOWNLOAD=0 to get an error instead). Datasets can also be downloaded from Python:

from pidsmaker.datasets import download

download("CADETS_E3", "LANL")  # returns the folders of the datasets

To build the datasets yourself, from the official DARPA files or the preprocessed files of LARES, see Building datasets from scratch.

items.title: 3. Log in to Weights & Biases
items.text:
PIDSMaker uses Weights & Biases (W&B) to log, plot and keep the history of experiments. We highly recommend it, but it is optional. Create an account, then log in with the API key from your W&B dashboard:

wandb login

Runs started with --wandb then send their logs and results to W&B.

items.title: Check your installation
items.text:
Run a first system on a dataset (downloaded first if needed):

ProvenanceNetwork 
pidsmaker velox CADETS_E3

pidsmaker euler LANL

If the pipeline starts building the graphs, you are all set. From a clone of the repository, python pidsmaker/main.py velox CADETS_E3 does the same. Continue with the Quickstart.

Something went wrong?

See FAQ & troubleshooting, or ask on Discord.

items.title: Where files are stored
items.text:
Files Default Change it with Datasets ~/.cache/pidsmaker/datasets/ --datasets_dir, or $PIDSMAKER_DATASETS_DIR Artifacts: everything a run produces (graphs, models, results...) /home/artifacts/ if this folder exists, else artifacts/ in the folder where you run pidsmaker --artifact_dir, or $PIDSMAKER_ARTIFACT_DIR

Artifacts take much more space than datasets: point them to a large disk. Set PIDSMAKER_ARTIFACT_DIR rather than relying on the working directory, so that all your runs share the cache of their tasks. All the environment variables are listed in the command line reference.

items.title: macOS
items.text:
PyTorch 2.1.2 has wheels for Apple Silicon, so PIDSMaker installs as above. It runs on CPU: PIDSMaker does not use the GPU of Macs.

  • Memory. Runs on provenance datasets can take more than 15 GB of RAM, and the largest datasets (TRACE_E3 and the E5 datasets) need more memory and disk than a laptop has. PIDSMaker prints a warning at the beginning of a run when less than 16 GB are available. Graph construction uses less memory with fewer processes, e.g. --num_workers=2.
  • Port 5000 is used by AirPlay Receiver. Start the embedding visualizer on another port (--port 5001), or turn AirPlay Receiver off in System Settings > General > AirDrop & Handoff.

items.title: HPC clusters
items.text:
PIDSMaker needs nothing more on a cluster than on any Linux machine. On a login node, install it as above (load your cluster's conda module first if it has one). Home directories are often small: store the datasets and the artifacts on a large filesystem, e.g. your project or scratch space, in your ~/.bashrc or job scripts:

export PIDSMAKER_DATASETS_DIR=/path/to/large/disk/pidsmaker/datasets
export PIDSMAKER_ARTIFACT_DIR=/path/to/large/disk/pidsmaker/artifacts

Compute nodes often have no internet access. From a login node, download the datasets, and the NLTK tokenizer data that PIDSMaker otherwise downloads the first time it is imported:

pidsmaker download CADETS_E3 THEIA_E3
python -m nltk.downloader punkt

In your jobs, activate the environment, set PIDSMAKER_AUTO_DOWNLOAD=0 (a missing dataset then stops the run with an error, instead of a download attempt), and run pidsmaker SYSTEM DATASET.

items.title: Quickstart
items.text:
This page shows how to run the existing systems, provenance-based (PIDSs) and network (NIDSs), change their arguments from the command line, and find their results.

Before you start

Complete the installation. The pidsmaker command runs from any folder.

items.title: Your first run
items.text:
Every run takes the same two positional arguments, a system and a dataset:

pidsmaker SYSTEM DATASET [--arg=value ...]

From a clone of the repository, python pidsmaker/main.py SYSTEM DATASET [--arg=value ...] is equivalent.

SYSTEM

The name of a YAML file in config/, which describes the full pipeline of a system:

  • provenance: velox, orthrus, kairos, magic, flash, nodlink, rcaid, threatrace, ocrapt;
  • network: euler, argus, jbeil, lares, egraphsage, anomal_e;
  • or your own.

See Systems for a comparison.

DATASET

A dataset defined in DATASET_DEFAULT_CONFIG in pidsmaker/config/config.py, which maps it to its database, a folder of Parquet files downloaded the first time the dataset is used:

  • provenance: CADETS_E3, THEIA_E3, CLEARSCOPE_E3, FIVEDIRECTIONS_E3, TRACE_E3, CADETS_E5, THEIA_E5, CLEARSCOPE_E5, FIVEDIRECTIONS_E5, TRACE_E5, optc_h201, optc_h501, optc_h051, ATLASV2_EDR, CARBANAKV2_EDR;
  • network: LANL, OPTC_NET.

See Datasets.

Any system runs on both kinds of datasets, with a few exceptions.

For example:

ProvenanceNetwork

Velox on CADETS E3, which looks for the processes, files and netflows of the attacks:

pidsmaker velox CADETS_E3

Euler on LANL, which looks for the authentications of the red team:

pidsmaker euler LANL

The content of the config (e.g. config/velox.yml) is parsed and checked against the arguments available in TASK_ARGS (pidsmaker/config/config.py), then the seven stages of the pipeline run one after the other.

items.title: Ways to run
items.text:
ShellShell + W&BBackground + W&B

Logs are printed to the terminal. Good for quick tests and debugging.

pidsmaker SYSTEM DATASET

Same, but logs, metrics and figures are also sent to Weights & Biases.

pidsmaker SYSTEM DATASET --wandb

Recommended for research and for running several experiments in parallel. The run continues after you close the terminal or log out, and logs to W&B. The command prints the log file of the run, in the current folder:

pidsmaker SYSTEM DATASET --wandb --background
tail -f pidsmaker_SYSTEM_DATASET_*.log   # follow the logs

All runs of pidsmaker are reproducible: it sets PYTHONHASHSEED=0 (sets of strings are iterated in the same order) and CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8 (for the deterministic algorithms of CUDA), unless you set them yourself. python pidsmaker/main.py does not.

items.title: Change arguments
items.text:
Every argument of the YAML config can be overridden from the command line, using its dotted path. CLI arguments always take precedence over the YAML file:

ProvenanceNetwork 
pidsmaker kairos CADETS_E3 \
  --training.node_hid_dim=128 \
  --batching.intra_graph_batching.tgn_last_neighbor.tgn_neighbor_size=10

pidsmaker euler LANL \
  --construction.time_window_size=60.0 \
  --training.decoder.predict_edge_contrastive.neg_ratio=5

Components can be swapped the same way. For example, Orthrus with doc2vec instead of word2vec, and 3 GraphSAGE layers instead of 2 attention layers:

pidsmaker orthrus CADETS_E3 \
  --featurization.used_method=doc2vec \
  --featurization.emb_dim=128 \
  --training.encoder.used_methods=tgn,sage \
  --training.encoder.sage.num_layers=3

All arguments are listed in the Reference. The flags that are not part of the YAML config (--wandb, --cpu, --force_restart...) are listed in Command line.

Re-running is cheap

Each task of the pipeline is cached on disk under a hash of its arguments. When you change --training.lr, graph construction and featurization are reused and only training and evaluation run again. See Pipeline.

items.title: GPU or CPU
items.text:
By default, PIDSMaker runs on the GPU cuda:0. If no GPU is found, it falls back to the CPU and prints a warning. To force the CPU:

pidsmaker velox CADETS_E3 --cpu

items.title: Results
items.text:
At the end of the evaluation task, metrics are printed in the logs and, with --wandb, sent to W&B with the figures (score distributions, detected attacks...). The main metrics are:

Metric Meaning precision, recall, fscore, mcc Classification of nodes (or edges, time windows) as malicious, with the threshold chosen on the validation set tp, fp, tn, fn Confusion matrix ap, auc Average precision and ROC AUC of the anomaly scores, independent of the threshold adp_score Attack Detection Precision: area under the curve of the percentage of attacks detected against precision. It rewards systems that detect every attack with few false positives discrimination Margin between the highest score of each attack and the mean of the 10 highest benign scores (normalized scores), averaged over attacks. Positive when attacks stand out

Provenance systems classify nodes by default, network systems edges (authentications or flows). How samples are labeled, how thresholds are chosen and how each metric is computed is explained in Evaluation & labeling.

All files produced by a run are written in the artifact folder: $PIDSMAKER_ARTIFACT_DIR if it is set, else /home/artifacts/ if this folder exists, else artifacts/ in the working directory. Use --artifact_dir to change it for a run (see Where files are stored).
