items.title: Encoders
items.text:
Encoders compute the node (and edge) embeddings that are passed to the decoders, whose outputs feed the objectives that compute the loss. They can be GNNs that leverage the graph structure (tgn, graph_attention, sage...), but also a single linear layer like in Velox (none) or a custom MLP (custom_mlp). Several encoders can be chained with training.encoder.used_methods, e.g. tgn,graph_attention.

The main encoders, grouped by what they model, with the systems that use them:

Role Encoders Used by Message passing within each graph sage, gat, graph_attention, gin, gcn, sum_aggregation, rcaid_gat, magic_gat Flash and ThreaTrace (sage), Kairos, Orthrus and Jbeil (graph_attention), Euler (gcn), NodLink, R-Caid, MAGIC Edge types and attributes in messages rgcn, rgcn_per_type, argus, egraphsage, lares, gin (GINE, with edge features), shadewatcher OCR-APT (rgcn_per_type), Argus, E-GraphSAGE and Anomal-E (egraphsage), LARES, ShadeWatcher Identity of each node node_id_embedding, lares Euler, Argus, LARES Memory across time windows tgn, snapshot_gru Kairos, Orthrus and Jbeil (tgn), Euler and Argus (snapshot_gru) Sequence of whole-graph embeddings textrcnn ProGrapher No message passing none (linear layer), custom_mlp Velox Heterogeneous graphs hetero_graph_transformer

Encoders that learn the identity of nodes are meant for nodes without informative features, such as the hosts of network datasets; encoders that read edge attributes need a dataset that has some, or the edge type in their place (batching.edge_features=edge_type). Any encoder can otherwise be used on provenance and network datasets.

hetero_graph_transformer is a Heterogeneous Graph Transformer (HGT): each node type and edge type gets its own attention parameters. It is not available on OpTC.

gcn Graph convolutional layers whose edges are weighted by batch.edge_weight, set by the merge_edges transformation (Euler). argus GCN layers followed by an edge-conditioned convolution (NNConv) on the edge features, if any (Argus). lares A learned embedding of each host's identity, then a single sum-aggregation layer over the messages of the neighbors and the features of their edges (LARES). flow sets the direction of aggregation, and use_node_features adds the node features to the ID embedding. egraphsage GraphSAGE layers whose messages include the edge features, aggregated in both directions with undirected (E-GraphSAGE, Anomal-E). shadewatcher The recommendation model of ShadeWatcher on a knowledge graph whose triples are the edges, with the edge type and an interact relation. Entities are embedded by a linear layer on their features (size node_hid_dim), and relations by TransR (kg_dim), trained by a pairwise loss against corrupted tails (kg_neg_ratio, kg_margin) that the encoder adds to the loss of the objectives. GNN layers (hidden_dims) then propagate the embeddings from the destinations of the edges of each node, weighted by the TransR attention of their triple, with a GraphSAGE aggregator; the output concatenates the entity embeddings with the normalized output of each layer, projected to node_out_dim if their sizes differ.

node_id_embedding and snapshot_gru wrap another encoder, like tgn (e.g. gcn,node_id_embedding,snapshot_gru), and can't be combined with tgn. node_id_embedding concatenates a learned embedding of each node's identity to its input features; with all_nodes, all the nodes of the dataset are embedded in every graph (edge-level objectives only). snapshot_gru runs a GRU over the successive embeddings of each node, one step per graph (Euler, Argus).

textrcnn The anomaly detector of ProGrapher. It does not embed nodes: it predicts the graph2vec embedding of each time window (featurization.used_method=graph2vec) from those of the last sequence_length windows, with a TextRCNN (bidirectional RNN of num_layers layers and size node_hid_dim, max-pooling, fully-connected layer). Like snapshot_gru, it keeps a state across graphs (the last embeddings), reset before each training epoch; with fewer previous windows, the sequence is shorter. It requires one graph per time window (no global, intra- or inter-graph batching) and the predict_snapshot_embedding objective.

items.title: Featurization
items.text:
Featurization methods are used to transform textual attributes of entities (e.g. file paths, process command lines, socket IP addresses and ports) into a vector. Some methods like word2vec and doc2vec learn this vector from the text corpus, while others like hierarchical_hashing compute the vector in a deterministic way.

Other methods like only_type and only_ones simply skip this embedding step and assign either a one-hot encoded type or ones to each entity. Those methods thus do not require any specific argument. In all methods, the resulting vectors are used as node features during the training task.

The graph2vec method (ProGrapher) embeds each time-window graph as a whole rather than its nodes: the Weisfeiler-Lehman rooted subgraphs of all nodes, built from node and edge types up to depth wl_iterations, are the words of a document embedded with doc2vec (PV-DBOW). The model is trained on the snapshots of training_split, then the embedding of every snapshot is inferred (infer_epochs) and stored in its graph, with the rooted subgraphs of its nodes; nodes only get their type as features. It is used by the textrcnn encoder and the predict_snapshot_embedding objective.

The pretrained method uses an encoder pretrained on provenance data (SPIDER, language models, self-supervised GNNs, …), selected with pretrained.model_type. See Pretrained Encoders.

Network datasets

The nodes of network datasets are hosts, labelled by their name or ID (e.g. C1065 in LANL). Text methods run on them (Velox uses word2vec on LANL), but these labels carry little information: the network systems use only_type or only_ones, and learn the identity of each host in their encoder (node_id_embedding, lares). fasttext stops with an error when no token appears min_count times, which happens with unique host names.

The attributes of events (logon types, ports, protocols, sizes...) are not featurized here: feat_inference encodes them as edge features (one-hot categorical and log-scaled numeric attributes), used with batching.edge_features=edge_attrs and selected with feat_inference.edge_attributes.

items.title: Tokenization
items.text:
Methods that learn from text first split the label of each entity into tokens. The tokenization is set in featurization.tokenization, independently of the featurization method: used_method selects the tokenizer and the sub-dict of the same name sets its arguments. Each system config sets its own tokenization, so it is reproduced exactly, and any featurization method can use the tokenization of another system.

Tokenization Splits labels into Used by nltk words, with NLTK, after separating paths on / and IPs on : and . (type_aware: True), or every label on /, : and . (type_aware: False) Orthrus, R-Caid, NodLink (type_aware: True), FLASH (type_aware: False) hierarchical each level of the path or IP: /usr/bin/ls → /usr, /usr/bin, /usr/bin/ls Kairos whole_label a single token per entity (type and label) DeepWalk, Node2Vec bpe domain-specific pieces (path components, flags, ports, IP categories, …) and BPE subwords learned on the training labels SPIDER and the other pretrained encoders huggingface the subwords of a HuggingFace tokenizer (model_name) GPT-2, Llama and OPT pretrained encoders none no tokens methods that do not read labels: only_type, only_ones, magic, ocrapt_features, alacarte, graph2vec

For example, Orthrus with the BPE tokenization of SPIDER:

pidsmaker orthrus CADETS_E3 --featurization.tokenization.used_method=bpe

doc2vec, temporal_rw, flash and hierarchical_hashing accept every tokenization except none. word2vec and fasttext also exclude whole_label, since they learn from one sentence per label. The BPE vocabulary is learned on the same labels as the featurization method and saved with it. The pretrained encoders are built around one tokenization, which must match pretrained.model_type.

featurization:
  tokenization:
    used_method: nltk
    nltk:
      type_aware: True
      substitutions: none

items.title: Substitutions
items.text:
Some values change between otherwise identical entities: hashes, UUIDs, random temporary file names, PIDs, ephemeral ports. Each tokenization sets in substitutions which of them are replaced by a placeholder token before tokenizing, so that such entities share their tokens. It is a comma-separated list, or none:

Substitution Replaces Placeholder hash hexadecimal strings of 7+ characters (MD5, SHA, commit ids) [HASH] guid GUIDs / UUIDs, also inside a word [GUID] random random-looking strings (mixed case and digits) and Windows SIDs [RANDOM] version version numbers (1.2.3, v2.0-rc1) [VER] timestamp words starting with a date (2019-05-08...) [TIMESTAMP] env_var environment variables ($HOME, ${PATH}, %APPDATA%) [ENV] number numbers above 255 (PIDs, inodes); smaller ones like IP octets are kept [NUM] ip IP addresses of netflow entities [PRIVATE_IP], [PUBLIC_IP], [LOCALHOST_IP] port ports of netflow entities [PORT_HTTPS], [PORT_SSH], … or [PORT_LOW], [PORT_REG], [PORT_EPH]

The original systems use none, except SPIDER and the other BPE-based pretrained encoders, which use all of them. For example, Orthrus with hashes, random strings and large numbers replaced:

pidsmaker orthrus CADETS_E3 --featurization.tokenization.nltk.substitutions="hash, random, number"

The bpe tokenization applies them during its domain-specific pre-tokenization (mode: domain_bpe), where they are checked on each path component and argument. The other tokenizations apply them to whole words of the label, separated by spaces and by / \ : = , & (by spaces and ip:port in netflow labels), before tokenizing it; placeholders are kept as single tokens.

items.title: Objectives
items.text:
An objective consists of a loss function and a decoder. Node-level objectives compute a loss for every node in a time-window graph, whereas edge-level ones compute a loss for every edge. This makes node-level objectives usually faster but less powerful than edge-level objectives to capture pair-wise information.

Level Objective Learns to Used by Edge predict_edge_type Predict the type of each edge Velox, Orthrus, Kairos Edge predict_edge_contrastive Tell real edges from negative ones (link prediction) Euler, Argus, Jbeil, E-GraphSAGE, ShadeWatcher Edge autoencode_edge_embeddings Reconstruct the embedding of each edge LARES Edge deep_graph_infomax Tell edges from those of a corrupted graph Anomal-E Edge reconstruct_edge_embeddings Reconstruct edge embeddings Edge predict_edge_supervised Separate benign edges from given attack edges Supervised fine-tuning Node predict_node_type Predict the type of each node Flash, ThreaTrace Node predict_process_tag Predict the name of the executable of each process, which is removed from its features (doc2vec.truncate_process_name); scores processes by the loss, or by the distance to K-Means clusters of training processes (detection: kmeans) R-Caid Node reconstruct_node_features, reconstruct_node_embeddings Reconstruct node features or embeddings NodLink Node reconstruct_masked_features, predict_masked_struct Reconstruct masked features and structure MAGIC Node one_class Map benign nodes into a hypersphere per node type (Deep SVDD) OCR-APT Node predict_snapshot_embedding Predict the graph2vec embedding of each time window; nodes are scored by their key indicators ProGrapher

Objectives are not tied to a family of datasets, except predict_node_type, which needs at least two node types: network datasets only have hosts (see Running across families for the combinations that are tested). On network datasets, predict_edge_type predicts the operation of events (e.g. LogOn), or the attribute set as edge type with construction.edge_type (e.g. logon_type).

predict_edge_contrastive Link prediction: the decoder scores the edges of the graph against negative edges. loss is bce (default), ap, the surrogate average precision loss of Argus, or bpr, the pairwise ranking loss of ShadeWatcher between each negative edge and the positive edge it was drawn for. neg_sampling draws the negatives: shuffle_dst (default) pairs each source with the destination of another edge, uniform and uniform_dst draw uniform nodes (neg_ratio negatives per edge), and tgn uses destinations embedded by the TGN (requires batching.intra_graph_batching.tgn_last_neighbor.negative_destinations). With the inner_product decoder, inner_product.negate scores edges by the negated inner product, as ShadeWatcher, whose inner product is the probability that two entities would not interact. autoencode_edge_embeddings The edge autoencoder of LARES: edge embeddings combine the embeddings of the two nodes with the edge features (gated skip connection, use_edge_feats), and edges are scored by their reconstruction error. deep_graph_infomax Deep Graph Infomax on edge embeddings, as in Anomal-E: edges are scored by the reconstruction error of their embedding by a PCA (pca_components) fitted on the training edges. predict_snapshot_embedding The objective of ProGrapher, used with the textrcnn encoder: the loss of a time window is the L2 distance between its graph2vec embedding and the embedding predicted from the previous windows. At inference, each node of the window gets the score of the window weighted by the rank of its key indicator: the rooted subgraphs (RSGs) of the window are ranked by how much more likely they are under the actual embedding than under the prediction, and a node gets score × (1 − rank / #RSGs) from the best-ranked RSG rooted at it. The maximum node score of a window is the window's score, so the same losses serve tw_evaluation and node_evaluation. With top_k, only the nodes of the top_k first RSGs keep a score. Its validation score (best_model_selection: best_val_score) is the opposite of the mean validation error.

autoencode_edge_embeddings, deep_graph_infomax and predict_snapshot_embedding have no decoder (decoder: none).

predict_edge_type also accepts loss: AMS, an additive margin softmax configured in its AMS section.

predict_edge_supervised is the only supervised objective: it learns from attack edges that you provide. See Supervised Fine-Tuning.

items.title: Tasks
items.text:
Every argument of each pipeline task, as accepted in a system's YAML config or on the command line (e.g. --training.lr=0.001).

How to read this page

  • Keys are nested exactly as in the YAML config. On the CLI, join them with dots: training.encoder.dropout → --training.encoder.dropout=0.3.
  • Click the markers to see a description and the allowed values of an argument.
  • Arguments of interchangeable methods (featurization methods, encoders, decoders, objectives, cleaning) are documented on their own pages: Featurization, Encoders, Decoders, Objectives, Cleaning.

Generated content

The argument lists below are generated from TASK_ARGS in pidsmaker/config/config.py by docs/scripts/get_arguments.py. Don't edit them by hand.

items.title: Stage 1: Construction
items.text:
Builds the time-window graphs of provenance or network events from the database. The raw data can be cleaned before the graphs are built with construction.cleaning: see Cleaning.

  • used_method: str (1)
  • use_all_files: bool
  • mimicry_edge_num: int
  • time_window_size: float (2)
  • use_hashed_label: bool (3)
  • fuse_edge: bool (4)
  • consistent_edge_types: bool (5)
  • operations: str (6)
  • drop_noise_events: bool (7)
  • benign_training: bool (8)
  • edge_type: str (9)
  • node_label_features
    • subject: str (10)

    • netflow: str (12)
    • host: str (13)
  • null_label_tokens: bool (14)
  • multi_dataset: str (15)

  1. The method to build time window graphs.Available options (one selection):defaultmagic
  2. The size of each graph in minutes. The notation should always be float (e.g. 10.0). Supports sizes < 1.0.
  3. Whether to hash the textual features.
  4. Whether to fuse duplicate sequential edges into a single edge.
  5. Map OpTC edge types to DARPA TC equivalents for shared vocabulary across datasets.
  6. Events kept when building graphs, by value of their operation column: default keeps the default events of the dataset's schema (all events, except for OpTC network flows where only FLOW_START events are kept, as in LARES and Argus), all keeps all events, otherwise a comma-separated list of operations (e.g. FLOW_START,FLOW_MESSAGE).
  7. Drops the noise events of the dataset's schema when building graphs (OpTC network flows: NetBIOS, LLMNR and SSDP broadcasts and multicasts and ICMPv6 neighbor discovery, which link every host to most hosts in every time window). No effect on datasets without noise events. Default: True.
  8. Drops the events labelled malicious from the graphs of the train and val dates, so that models are trained and validated on benign events only (datasets with event labels whose train or val dates have attacks). No effect on other datasets and dates. Default: True.
  9. Edge attribute used as edge type by graphs and models (e.g. the type predicted by predict_edge_type). operation is the default type of events of the dataset (e.g. system calls in provenance datasets), other values are categorical edge attributes of the dataset's schema (e.g. logon_type in LANL).Available options (one selection):auth_typedst_portdst_user_kindlogon_typeoperationprotocolsrc_portsrc_user_kindsuccess
  10. Attributes of subject nodes used as node labels (concatenated): path, cmd_line. type adds the node type, and auto uses the type-specific default label, only made of non-null attributes.Available options (multi selection):autotypepathcmd_line
  11. Attributes of file nodes used as node labels (concatenated): path. type adds the node type, and auto uses the type-specific default label, only made of non-null attributes.Available options (multi selection):autotypepath
  12. Attributes of netflow nodes used as node labels (concatenated): local_ip, local_port, remote_ip, remote_port. type adds the node type, and auto uses the type-specific default label, only made of non-null attributes.Available options (multi selection):autotypelocal_iplocal_portremote_ipremote_port
  13. Attributes of host nodes used as node labels (concatenated): name. type adds the node type, and auto uses the type-specific default label, only made of non-null attributes.Available options (multi selection):autotypename
  14. When enabled, null entity attributes produce explicit tokens ([NO_CMD], [NO_PATH], [NO_IP]) instead of empty strings.
  15. A comma-separated list of datasets on which training is performed. Evaluation is done only the primary dataset run in CLI.Available options (one selection):THEIA_E5THEIA_E3CADETS_E5CADETS_E3CLEARSCOPE_E5CLEARSCOPE_E3optc_h201optc_h501optc_h051TRACE_E5TRACE_E3FIVEDIRECTIONS_E5FIVEDIRECTIONS_E3PROVENANCE_BENIGNATLASV2_EDRCARBANAKV2_EDRLANLOPTC_NETnone

Cleaning methods applied to the raw data before building the graphs, or none. remove_null_attributes: null-like attributes (None, NA, <UNNAMED fd:3>, invalid IPs and ports) are removed from labels; normalize_labels: whitespaces, slashes, path prefixes and quotes are normalized and long labels truncated; remove_duplicate_events: events with the same source, destination, type and timestamp are kept once; remove_self_loops: events from a node to itself are removed; remove_noisy_netflows: netflows to multicast/broadcast/... IPs are removed with their events; dedup_window_edges: only the first event of each (source, destination, type) is kept in each time window.Available options (multi selection):remove_null_attributesnormalize_labelsremove_duplicate_eventsremove_self_loopsremove_noisy_netflowsdedup_window_edgesnone

items.title: Stage 2: Transformation
items.text:
Optional transformations applied to the graphs after construction.

  • used_methods: str (1)
  • rcaid_pseudo_graph
    • use_pruning: bool (2)
    • prune_threshold: float (3)
    • root_node_types: str (4)
    • keep_original_edges: bool (5)
    • merge_same_label_roots: bool (6)

  • merge_edges
    • per_edge_type: bool (8)

  • synthetic_attack_naive

    • num_malicious_process: int

  1. Applies transformations to graphs after their construction. Multiple transformations can be applied sequentially. Example: used_methods=undirected,dagAvailable options (multi selection):undirecteddagrcaid_pseudo_graphmerge_edgesnonesynthetic_attack_naive
  2. Whether roots reaching more than prune_threshold of the nodes of the graph get no pseudo edges (R-Caid's pruning of highly-connected roots).
  3. Fraction of the nodes of the graph above which the descendants of a root are pruned (0.5 for DARPA TC in the paper).
  4. Comma-separated node types that can be roots (e.g. file,netflow: files and sockets, as in the paper), or all.
  5. Whether the transformed graph keeps the edges of the provenance graph next to the pseudo edges (root -> descendant), which have no edge type. If False, only the pseudo edges are kept.
  6. Whether the pseudo edges of the roots with the same type and label (thus the same features) towards a same node are merged into one, from the first such root.
  7. Maximum number of pseudo-roots of a node (0: no limit): its roots with the fewest descendants. Bounds the pseudo edges by this number times the number of nodes, e.g. when a process reads thousands of files that become roots of all its descendants.
  8. Whether repeated edges are merged per edge type (one edge per source, destination and type) or regardless of their type (one edge per source and destination, as in Euler). Merged edges have a count and a weight attribute.
  9. Whether the edge attributes of a merged edge (batching.edge_features=edge_attrs) aggregate all its events, as the edge features of Euler, Argus and LARES: the number of events, the number of events with each value of each categorical attribute (e.g. successful and failed logons) and the number, mean and std of the values of numeric attributes, each standardized over the edges of the graph as sigmoid(floor(x / std)). Otherwise, the attributes of the first event are kept.

items.title: Feature inference
items.text:
feat_inference runs right after featurization and embeds every node of the graphs with the trained model. Its arguments mostly apply to pretrained encoders: continued pretraining on the target dataset, and the renaming attack.

  • to_remove: bool
  • edge_attributes: str (1)
  • continue_pretrain: bool (2)
  • continue_pretrain_epochs: int (3)
  • continue_pretrain_lr_factor: float (4)
  • edge_batch_size: int (5)
  • rename_attack
    • enabled: bool (6)
    • entities: str (7)
    • target_node_type: str (8)
    • top_k: int (9)
    • target_label: str (10)
    • seed: int (11)
  1. Edge attributes of the dataset's schema used as edge features (batching.edge_features=edge_attrs): all, a comma-separated list of attribute names (names absent from the dataset are ignored), or lists per dataset, e.g. LANL:success;OPTC_NET:src_port,dst_port,protocol (unlisted datasets use all their attributes).
  2. Continue pretraining on the target dataset before inference. Default: False.
  3. Number of epochs for continue-pretraining on target dataset. Default: 3.
  4. LR multiplier relative to original peak LR (e.g., 0.1 = 10x lower). Default: 0.1.
  5. Number of edges to process in each batch during feat_inference. Default: 5000.
  6. If True, after embeddings are computed, replace the embedding of selected test-set nodes with a benign target embedding. Simulates an inference-time renaming/mimicry attack.
  7. Comma-separated BASE NAMES of attack entities (e.g. 'main, XIM, sendmail'). Each is matched two ways against test-set nodes of target_node_type: (a) exact label equality, and (b) labels ending with '/' (path-style).
  8. Node type the attack targets (only nodes of this type are rewritten).Available options (one selection):subjectfilenetflow
  9. If >0, automatically build a benign-target pool from the top-K most frequent BARE labels (no '/') of target_node_type seen in the training split, and assign one target per attack entity. Path-suffix matches preserve the original prefix (e.g. '/tmp/main' -> '/tmp/'). If 0, use the manual target_label for every entity (e.g. for an 'unseen-by-pretraining' target).
  10. (Manual mode only, used when top_k=0) Bare base name to replace every attack entity. Path-suffix matches still preserve the prefix (e.g. '/tmp/main' -> '/tmp/').
  11. Seed used to shuffle the auto-picked benign pool before assigning one target per entity. Vary it for sensitivity analysis over which benign label each malicious entity is mimicking.

  • intra_graph_batching
    • used_methods: str (11)
    • edges
      • intra_graph_batch_size: int (12)
    • tgn_last_neighbor

      • tgn_neighbor_n_hop: int (14)

      • fix_tgn_neighbor_loader: bool (16)
      • directed: bool (17)
      • insert_neighbors_before: bool (18)
      • reset_state_every_day: bool (19)
      • negative_destinations: bool (20)
  • inter_graph_batching
    • used_method: str (21)
    • inter_graph_batch_size: int (22)
  1. Whether to store the graphs on disk upon building the graphs. Used to avoid re-computation of very complex batching operations that take time. Can take up to 300GB storage for CADETS_E5.
  2. Node features to use during GNN training. node_type is a one-hot encoded entity type vector, node_emb refers to the embedding generated during the featurization task, only_ones is a vector of ones with length node_type, edges_distribution counts emitted and received edges.Available options (multi selection):node_typenode_embonly_onesedges_distribution
  3. Scaling of the edges_distribution counts: max divides them by the largest count of the time window (default), none keeps the raw counts (as ThreaTrace), log1p applies log(1 + x).Available options (one selection):maxnonelog1p
  4. Edge features to used during GNN training. edge_type refers to the system call type, edge_type_triplet considers a same edge type as a new type if source or destination node types are different, msg is the message vector used in the TGN, time_encoding encodes temporal order of events with their timestamps in the TGN, edge_attrs are the edge attributes of the dataset's schema besides the edge type (one-hot categorical and log-scaled numeric attributes, e.g. ports or logon types), none uses no features.Available options (multi selection):edge_typeedge_type_tripletmsgtime_encodingedge_attrsnone
  5. Whether the GNN should be trained on all datasets in multi_dataset.
  6. Renumbers the nodes of the graphs from 0 to (number of nodes in the graphs - 1), keeping their order, instead of using the node IDs of the database, which also count the nodes absent from all graphs (86% of the 44.5M IDs of TRACE_E3). Tensors indexed by node (TGN memory, neighbor loader, node ID embeddings, all_nodes embeddings, ...) are sized accordingly. Node IDs are restored in the outputs. Results are unchanged, except for methods drawing random nodes among all IDs (e.g. uniform negatives of Euler and Argus).
  7. A bug has been found in the first version of the framework, where reindexing graphs in shape (N, d) slightly modify node features. Setting this to true fixes the bug.
  8. Flattens the time window-based graphs into a single large temporal graph and recreate graphs based on the given method. edges creates contiguous graphs of size global_batching_batch_size edges, the same applies for minutes, unique_edge_types builds graphs where each pair of connected nodes share edges with distinct edge types, none uses the default time window-based batching defined in minutes with arg time_window_size.Available options (one selection):edgesminutesunique_edge_typesnone
  9. Controls the value associated with global_batching.used_method (training+inference).
  10. Controls the value associated with global_batching.used_method (inference only).
  11. Breaks each previously computed graph into even smaller graphs. edges creates contiguous graphs of size intra_graph_batch_size edges (if a graph has 2000 edges and intra_graph_batch_size=1500 creates two graphs: one with 1500 edges, the other with 500 edges), tgn_last_neighbor computes for each graph its associated graph based on the TGN last neighbor loader, namely a new graph where each node is connected with its last tgn_neighbor_size incoming edges. none does not alter any graph.Available options (multi selection):edgestgn_last_neighbornone
  12. Controls the value associated with global_batching.used_method.
  13. Number of last neighbors to store for each node.
  14. If greater than one, will also gather the last neighbors of neighbors.
  15. A bug has been in the first version of the framework, where the features of last neighbors not appearing in the input graph have zero node feature vectors. Setting this arg to true includes the features of all nodes in the TGN graph.
  16. We found a minor bug in the original TGN code (https://github.com/pyg-team/pytorch_geometric/issues/10100). This is an unofficial fix.
  17. The original TGN's loader builds graphs in an undirected way. This makes the graphs purely directed.
  18. Whether to insert the edges of the current graph before loading last neighbors.
  19. Empties the last neighbors and resets the TGN memory at the first batch of each day (date of its first event), as Kairos, which trains and tests on one graph per day.
  20. Draws a negative destination for each edge, uniformly among the destinations of the training graphs (training) or of all graphs (validation, test), and adds it to the nodes of the TGN graph to be embedded with memory and neighbors, as TGN and Jbeil (used by predict_edge_contrastive.neg_sampling=tgn).
  21. Batches multiple graphs into a single large one for parallel training. Does not support TGN. graph_batching batches inter_graph_batch_size together, none doesn't batch graphs.Available options (one selection):graph_batchingnone
  22. Controls the value associated with inter_graph_batching.used_method.

  • evaluate_selected_epoch_only: bool (3)
  • save_figures: bool (4)
  • best_model_selection: str (5)

  • node_evaluation
    • threshold_method: str (6)

      • alpha: float (7)

    • use_kmeans: bool (9)
    • kmeans_top_K: int (10)
    • ocrapt_contamination: float (11)
    • ocrapt_min_contamination: float (12)
    • magic_knn_k: int (13)
    • magic_max_reference_size: int (14)
    • magic_embedding: str (15)
  • tw_evaluation
    • threshold_method: str (16)
  • node_tw_evaluation
    • threshold_method: str (17)
    • use_dst_node_loss: bool
    • use_kmeans: bool
    • kmeans_top_K: int
  • queue_evaluation
    • used_method: str (18)
    • queue_threshold: int
    • kairos_idf_queue
      • include_test_set_in_IDF: bool
    • provnet_lof_queue
      • queue_arg: str
  • host_two_stage_evaluation
    • alpha: int (19)
    • beta: int (20)
    • root_attack_nodes: str (21)
    • test_end: str (22)
  • edge_evaluation
    • malicious_edge_selection: str (23)

  1. Whether to generate images of malicious nodes' neighborhoods (not stable).
  2. Available options (one selection):orthrusreaprthreatrace
  3. Only evaluates the epoch selected by a label-free best_model_selection (last_epoch, best_val_score), instead of evaluating every epoch on the test set (faster on large test sets, without per-epoch test metrics).
  4. Whether to save the figures of the evaluation (scores, ADP and discrimination curves) for each evaluated epoch. Metrics are computed either way. Figures with one point per edge or node are slow to draw on large test sets.
  5. Strategy to select the best model across epochs. best_adp selects the best model based on the highest ADP score, best_discrimination selects the model that does the best separation between top-score TPs and top-score FPs. These two use test labels. best_val_score selects the model with the best score on validation data computed by the objective (link prediction AUC + AP of validation edges for predict_edge_contrastive), as Euler's early stopping. last_epoch selects the last evaluated epoch (no labels used). best_mcc selects the best MCC on the test set (as LARES' code).Available options (one selection):best_adpbest_discriminationbest_ap@10best_val_scorebest_mcclast_epoch
  6. Method to calculate the threshold value used to detect anomalies.Available options (one selection):max_val_lossmean_val_losspercentilethreatracemagicflashnodlinkfixed_zeroocrapt
  7. Weights the margin applied to the threshold value.
  8. Whether to consider the loss of destination nodes when computing the node-level scores (maximum loss of a node).
  9. Whether to cluster nodes after thresholding as done in Orthrus
  10. Number of top-score nodes selected before clustering.
  11. For threshold_method=ocrapt: max per-type contamination (top fraction flagged), clamped from that type's own val malicious fraction.
  12. For threshold_method=ocrapt: min per-type contamination floor.
  13. For threshold_method=magic: number of nearest benign training nodes whose mean distance scores a test node (default 10, as in the MAGIC paper).
  14. For threshold_method=magic: the k-NN reference set is a random sample of at most this many benign training node embeddings (0: all of them).
  15. For threshold_method=magic: node embedding scored by the k-NN detector, the output of the last encoder layer (last, MAGIC's code) or the concatenation of all its layers (concat, MAGIC's paper).Available options (one selection):lastconcat
  16. Time-window detection: each test time window is scored by reducing the losses of its edges, and classified as malicious if its score exceeds the threshold.Available options (one selection):max_val_lossmean_val_losspercentilethreatracemagicflashnodlinkfixed_zeroocrapt
  17. Node-level detection where a same node in multiple time windows is considered as multiple unique nodes. More realistic evaluation for near real-time detection.Available options (one selection):max_val_lossmean_val_losspercentilethreatracemagicflashnodlinkfixed_zeroocrapt

Queue-level detection as in Kairos: anomalous time windows sharing rare (high-IDF) nodes are grouped into queues, and the time windows of queues whose anomaly score exceeds queue_threshold are flagged. provnet_lof_queue is not supported anymore.Available options (one selection):kairos_idf_queueprovnet_lof_queue

  22. End of the evaluated test period (%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S in the dataset's timezone). Empty: the whole test period.
  23. The ground truth only contains node-level labels. This arg controls the strategy to label edges. src_nodes and dst_nodes consider an edge as malicious if only its source or only its destination node is malicious. both labels an edge as malicious if both end nodes are malicious.Available options (one selection):src_nodedst_nodeboth_nodes
